title: Dental polyclinic, clinic or private practice in Beylikdüzü: what's the difference?
desc: The difference between a dental polyclinic, a dental clinic and a private practice in Beylikdüzü: number of dentists, appointment flexibility, treatment plans and the questions to ask. Dent32 in Beylikdüzü is open seven days a week.
lead: In Turkey, a muayenehane (private practice) is opened by a single dentist in their own name, while a poliklinik (polyclinic) can be opened as a company and usually has several dentists working together. In everyday language, people call all of them a "dental clinic". When choosing in Beylikdüzü, what matters is not the sign above the door but the dental team, the written plan you get after the examination and the follow-up after treatment.

sections.h: Private practice, polyclinic and centre: what's the difference?
sections.html:
Private dental facilities in Turkey are regulated and licensed by the Ministry of Health. Roughly, the main types are:

TypeWho opens it?What it means in practice
Muayenehane (private practice)A dentist, in their own nameUsually one dentist; you often see the same dentist every time
Poliklinik (polyclinic)One or more dentists; can be a companySeveral dentists and chairs; appointment times can be more flexible
Oral and dental health centreA larger team and more dental chairsMany dentists, usually longer opening hours
HospitalAn in-patient facilityProcedures under general anaesthetic and extensive surgery

"Dental clinic" is the everyday word used for all of these. So searches for "dental clinic in Beylikdüzü" and "dental polyclinic in Beylikdüzü" usually show the same places. You can see a facility's licence type on the licence displayed at the entrance or simply ask.

In short

The word on the sign doesn't decide the quality of your treatment. Who will treat you, whether you get a written plan and who you can reach if something goes wrong matter far more.

sections.h: Advantages of a clinic with several dentists
sections.html:
• Team planning: When implants, orthodontics and aesthetic work come together in one mouth, it helps when dentists decide together. In smile design, for example, teeth may need straightening with braces or aligners before any crowns or veneers.
  • Flexible appointments: With several dentists and treatment rooms, weekend and evening appointments are easier to find.
  • Continuity: If one dentist is away, your records and treatment plan are still at the clinic when you come in with an urgent problem.
  • Second opinion: In complex cases, another dentist in the same clinic can give an opinion.

Single-dentist practices have strengths too: you see the same dentist each time and the relationship is more personal. The right choice depends on what you need.

desc: Emergency and on-call dentists in Beylikdüzü: the night and holiday rota at state dental facilities, which situations are truly urgent, when to call 112, and Dent32, open at weekends.
lead: With toothache that starts in the middle of the night, the first step is to tell pain apart from a spreading infection. If you have fast-growing facial swelling, difficulty swallowing or breathing, or a high fever, call 112 or go to a hospital emergency department straight away. Otherwise, controlling the pain until morning and seeing a dentist the same day is usually enough; Dent32 in Beylikdüzü is open every day, including weekends.

In short

An infection from a tooth spreading into the face and neck is rare but serious. With rapidly growing swelling and difficulty breathing, go straight to an emergency department, not a dental clinic.

sections.h: How does the on-call dentist system work?
sections.html:
In Istanbul, emergency dental care at night and on public holidays is mainly provided through the on-call rota of oral and dental health hospitals and centres run by the Ministry of Health. Because the facility on call can change from night to night, the most reliable way to find out is to check with the Istanbul Provincial Health Directorate or call the Ministry of Health helpline, ALO 184.

On-call services usually provide first aid that brings pain and infection under control: opening the tooth to relieve pressure, draining an abscess, stopping bleeding or, if needed, an extraction. Permanent treatments such as root canals, crowns or implants are planned at later appointments.

sections.h: What you can do at home until morning
sections.html:
• Painkillers: Take a painkiller your doctor has previously said is suitable for you, at the dose on the pack. Don't put aspirin on the tooth or gum; it burns the tissue.
  • Cold compress: A cold compress on the cheek for 15–20 minutes at a time can reduce swelling and pain. Avoid heat.
  • Keep your head up: Raising your head with an extra pillow when lying down can ease throbbing.
  • Warm salt water: For gum-related pain, gently rinsing with warm salt water can help.
  • Antibiotics: Don't start leftover antibiotics on your own. Antibiotics don't cure most toothache; we explain why in our article on antibiotics and toothache.

You'll find what to do for each type of pain in our night and weekend toothache guide.

faq.q: Do emergency departments treat teeth?

title: Tooth extraction and impacted wisdom teeth in Beylikdüzü: procedure, pain and recovery
desc: Tooth extraction and impacted wisdom tooth removal in Beylikdüzü: when a tooth needs to come out, how it's done, whether it hurts, blood thinners, recovery time and replacing the missing tooth.
lead: A tooth extraction is the removal, under local anaesthetic, of a tooth that is too damaged to save or is causing problems. A routine extraction usually takes a few minutes; an impacted wisdom tooth usually takes 20–45 minutes. You won't feel pain during the procedure; mild pain and swelling for the first 2–3 days is normal. At Dent32, we only decide on extraction after discussing options for saving the tooth.

sections.h: When does a tooth need to be extracted?
sections.html:
We aim to keep teeth wherever possible; decay or infection can often be treated with root canal treatment and a crown. Extraction usually comes up when:

  • The root is fractured or decay has reached the root and the tooth can't be restored
  • Advanced gum disease has destroyed the bone support and the tooth is loose
  • An impacted wisdom tooth causes repeated infection, decay in the neighbouring tooth or a cyst
  • Space is needed for orthodontic treatment
  • Infection persists despite treatment
In short

Before an extraction, we discuss options for saving the tooth and how the gap will be filled afterwards. If a gap is left for a long time, neighbouring teeth can drift and the bone shrinks.

sections.h: How is a tooth extracted, and does it hurt?
sections.html:
First, an X-ray is used to assess the root shape and surrounding structures. Local anaesthetic numbs the area completely; you may feel pressure but no pain. In a routine extraction, the tooth is gently loosened from its socket with special instruments and removed.

For impacted teeth or teeth with curved roots, the gum is opened, the tooth may be divided into pieces to remove it, and the area is closed with stitches. When patients tell us "I didn't feel a thing", it's mostly down to giving enough anaesthetic at the right time.

Type of extractionTypical timeRecovery
Routine (erupted tooth)A few minutes to 15 minutesSoft tissue about 1–2 weeks
Impacted or partially impacted wisdom toothAbout 20–45 minutesSwelling peaks at 2–3 days and clearly settles within a week
Multiple extractionsDepends on the number of teethPlanned together with dentures or implants

• Blood thinners: Don't stop aspirin, warfarin or newer anticoagulants on your own. The decision is made with the doctor who prescribed them; most extractions can be done safely while continuing the medicine, with local bleeding control.
  • Diabetes: If your blood sugar is under control, extraction is done as normal. Poorly controlled diabetes can delay healing.
  • Osteoporosis medicines: If you have taken bisphosphonates or similar medicines, always tell us; the plan is adjusted accordingly.
  • Pregnancy: Non-urgent extractions are usually postponed to the second trimester. Details: dental treatment during pregnancy.

• Bite on the gauze pad for 30–45 minutes.
  • For the first 24 hours, don't spit, use a straw or rinse; the clot could be dislodged.
  • Don't eat until the numbness wears off, and choose lukewarm, soft foods on the first day.
  • Smoking delays healing and raises the risk of dry socket; avoid it for at least 2–3 days.
  • Severe pain that gets worse after day 2–3, with a bad smell, may be dry socket; contact us.

For full details, see our after tooth extraction guide and our wisdom tooth article.

A gap can be filled with an implant, a bridge or a removable denture. In suitable cases an implant can be placed in the same session as the extraction. We compare the options in implant or bridge?.

faq.q: Does a tooth extraction hurt?
faq.a: Local anaesthetic means you won't feel pain during the procedure, although you may feel pressure. There is some mild pain once it wears off, usually controlled with painkillers.

faq.q: When can I go back to work after an extraction?

title: All-on-Four and full-arch implants in Beylikdüzü: the road to fixed teeth
desc: All-on-Four and full-arch implants in Beylikdüzü: who fixed teeth on four implants suit, whether same-day temporary teeth are possible, how many months it takes, how it compares with dentures, and aftercare. Dent32 Beylikdüzü.
lead: All-on-Four means placing four implants in a toothless jaw and fixing a one-piece row of teeth on top. If bone and general health allow, temporary fixed teeth can be fitted within a few days of implant surgery, often the same day; the final teeth are made after the implants have fused with the bone, usually within 3–6 months. At Dent32, the decision is made after a CT scan to assess the bone.

sections.h: What is All-on-Four, and how is it different from dentures?
sections.html:
A conventional full denture rests on the palate or gums and can move in the mouth. With All-on-Four, the prosthesis is screwed onto four implants; you don't take it in and out but clean it as you would your teeth. The back implants are usually placed at an angle, which keeps them away from the sinus and nerve and can reduce the need for bone grafting.

Conventional full dentureAll-on-Four
StabilityRemovable, may need adhesiveFixed, screwed onto implants
PalateUpper denture covers the palatePalate stays open, so taste and speech feel more natural
ChewingHard foods are difficultCloser to natural chewing
BoneBone continues to shrink over timeImplants load the bone and slow shrinkage
CareTaken out and cleanedCleaned in the mouth with a brush, interdental brush and water flosser

• People who have lost all their teeth, or whose remaining teeth can't be saved
  • Denture wearers who want fixed teeth
  • People whose general health allows minor surgery
  • People with enough bone to support at least four implants

Uncontrolled diabetes, heavy smoking and some bone medicines increase the risk; these are assessed in detail beforehand. See who can get dental implants. If bone is very limited, more than four implants (All-on-Six) or bone augmentation may be needed: bone grafts and sinus lifts.

1. Examination and 3D CT scan: Bone volume and distance to the sinus and nerve are measured.
  2. Digital planning: Implant positions and the length, colour and smile line of the teeth are planned.
  3. Surgery: Any extractions and placement of the four implants are done under local anaesthetic, usually in one session.
  4. Temporary fixed teeth: If the implants are stable enough at placement, a temporary row of teeth is fitted within a few days, often the same day.
  5. Integration: A soft diet for about 3–6 months.
  6. Final prosthesis: Impressions, try-in and fitting of the final row of teeth.
In short

Same-day temporary teeth aren't suitable for everyone. Whether the implants hold firmly enough at placement (primary stability) decides it.

We explain the general idea in our All-on-Four article and implant timelines in how long do implants take.

Food can collect under a fixed prosthesis. You need to brush twice a day, clean under the prosthesis with an interdental brush or water flosser, and have professional check-ups at least once or twice a year. At check-ups we monitor screw tightness, the gums and the bone around the implants. Inflammation around implants (peri-implantitis) is the main long-term threat; see how long do dental implants last for details.

At the examination we look at your bone, your expectations and your budget together, and set out All-on-Four, implant-retained removable dentures and conventional dentures side by side. The main cost factors are the implant brand, the prosthesis material (acrylic, zirconia or metal-reinforced) and any additional surgery. See implant-supported dentures and implant cost factors.

faq.q: How many days does All-on-Four take?
faq.a: Temporary fixed teeth are usually fitted within a few days of surgery. The final prosthesis is made after the implants fuse with the bone, usually within 3–6 months.

faq.q: Is All-on-Four painful?
faq.a: Surgery is done under local anaesthetic. There is swelling and tenderness for a few days afterwards, controlled with painkillers.

faq.q: Can I have All-on-Four if I don't have much bone?
faq.a: Angling the back implants often reduces the need for bone grafting. If bone is very insufficient, extra procedures or a different plan may be needed.

faq.q: Can both jaws be done at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. If your general health allows, both jaws can be planned in the same session or a short time apart.

faq.q: How long does a fixed prosthesis last?
faq.a: With good care, the implants can last for many years. The prosthetic teeth may wear over time and need replacing.

desc: What is a Hollywood smile, how is it done with veneers or zirconia, how many teeth are covered, are teeth filed down, and what makes it look natural? Planning and try-in at Dent32 in Beylikdüzü.
lead: A Hollywood smile means renewing all the teeth that show when you smile (usually 8–10 upper teeth, sometimes 16–20 including the lower jaw) at the same time with veneers or zirconia crowns, for a bright, even look. Whether it looks natural depends on choosing the colour, length and shape of the teeth to suit your face. sections.html:
Hollywood smile isn't a medical term but a description of a look: white, symmetrical, gap-free and even teeth. It's usually achieved with laminate veneers or zirconia crowns, sometimes planned together with whitening, gum contouring and orthodontics.

The real question isn't "how many teeth?" but which teeth show when you smile. With a broad smile, the premolars show too; covering only the front six teeth would leave a colour difference.

In short

A good Hollywood smile looks like healthy teeth, not "done" teeth. That comes from the right shade, tooth length that suits your facial proportions and a touch of natural translucency.

title: Dental fillings in Beylikdüzü: how long does a white filling take, and when can you eat?
desc: Dental fillings in Beylikdüzü: how a white (composite) filling is done, how long it takes, whether it hurts, when you can eat afterwards, how long fillings last and when an inlay or onlay is needed. Dent32.
lead: A filling replaces the cavity left after decay is removed with a tooth-coloured material. A single white (composite) filling usually takes 20–45 minutes and sets instantly under a curing light, so you only need to wait for the numbness to wear off before eating. Caught early, decay can be treated with a filling before it needs a root canal or crown.

sections.h: When do you need a filling?
sections.html:
Decay starts in the enamel (the outer layer) and, if untreated, moves into the dentine and then the nerve. Decay in the enamel and dentine is treated with a filling; once it reaches the nerve, root canal treatment is needed. We explain the stages in signs of tooth decay.

  • A brief twinge with sweet or cold things
  • Brown or black spots or a visible hole in the tooth
  • Food getting stuck between teeth
  • A chipped tooth edge or an old filling with an open margin
  • Decay between teeth seen on a check-up X-ray before it causes symptoms
In short

Decay found before it hurts ends with a small, inexpensive filling. That's why a check-up every 6–12 months is the way to catch fillings at the earliest stage.

sections.h: How is a white filling done?
sections.html:
1. If needed, the area is numbed with local anaesthetic.
  2. The decay is removed while sound tooth is preserved.
  3. The tooth surface is prepared with a special gel and bonding agent.
  4. The composite is matched to your tooth colour and built up in layers, each hardened with a blue curing light.
  5. The filling is shaped, the bite is checked and it's polished.

sections.h: When can I eat after a filling?
sections.html:
A composite filling sets instantly under the light, so there's no need to wait for the filling itself. If you had anaesthetic, though, don't eat until the numbness wears off (usually 1–3 hours); you could bite your cheek or lip without noticing. The same applies to hot drinks.

Mild sensitivity to cold for the first few days is normal. If the filling feels "high" when you bite, or sensitivity lasts more than a week, pop in for a quick adjustment. If a filling falls out, see what to do if a filling falls out.

sections.h: How long does a filling last?
sections.html:
Composite fillings usually last many years, depending on care, size and habits. The main things that shorten their life are clenching, biting hard objects, frequent sugary snacks and new decay at the edge of the filling. For very large losses, a porcelain or composite inlay or onlay made in a laboratory is a more durable option.

If your amalgam (silver) fillings are sound, you don't have to replace them just for colour; if they're cracked or decayed, they can be replaced with white fillings. Details: what is a white filling.

At the examination we check all your teeth and, if needed, take X-rays to see decay between teeth. If you need several fillings, we put them in order of urgency and plan them to reduce your number of visits. title: Scale and polish in Beylikdüzü: how often should you have it, and does it hurt?
desc: Scale and polish (professional teeth cleaning) in Beylikdüzü: how long it takes, whether it hurts or damages enamel, how often you need it, and sensitivity and gum bleeding afterwards. Dent32 Beylikdüzü.
lead: A scale and polish removes hardened plaque (tartar) from the teeth and along the gum line with ultrasonic instruments, then polishes the surface. It usually takes 30–45 minutes, doesn't damage enamel and is recommended every 6–12 months for most people. Tartar that a toothbrush can't remove is the most common cause of bleeding gums, bad breath and gum recession.

sections.html:
A layer of bacterial plaque forms on the teeth every day. Plaque that isn't removed by brushing and flossing hardens within a few days, combining with minerals in saliva to become tartar. Tartar is rough, so it holds even more plaque and constantly irritates the gums; once it has formed, brushing won't remove it.

The inner surfaces of the lower front teeth and the cheek side of the upper molars, close to the salivary glands, are where tartar builds up most.

In short

Tartar isn't just cosmetic. Left for a long time, gum inflammation can spread to the bone and teeth start to loosen.

sections.h: How is it done, and does it hurt?
sections.html:
1. Examination and gum measurements
  2. Removing tartar with an ultrasonic tip that breaks it up with vibration and water
  3. Fine cleaning with hand instruments
  4. Polishing the teeth smooth and reducing stains
  5. Advice on brushing and cleaning between teeth

Most people don't find it uncomfortable; you feel water and vibration. If the gums are very inflamed or teeth are sensitive, local anaesthetic or splitting the cleaning into several sessions may be preferred. Where gum pockets are deep, a deep clean of the root surfaces is needed; see gum treatment in Beylikdüzü.

No. Ultrasonic instruments break up hard tartar; used correctly, they don't wear away healthy enamel. The feeling that the gaps between your teeth have "opened up" afterwards comes from the tartar that filled those gaps being removed; the tartar created the space in the first place by pushing the gum back. faq.a: Usually 30–45 minutes. With heavy tartar or inflamed gums, more than one session may be needed.

faq.q: Does a scale and polish hurt?
faq.a: For most people it doesn't; you feel water and vibration. Local anaesthetic can be used for sensitive teeth.

faq.q: Why are my teeth sensitive after cleaning?
faq.a: Surfaces previously covered by tartar are exposed, so sensitivity for a day or two is possible. A sensitive-teeth toothpaste helps.

faq.q: Does a scale and polish whiten teeth?
faq.a: It removes stains and tartar, so teeth look lighter, but it doesn't change the tooth's own colour. That needs whitening.

faq.a: Yes. Gum bleeding can increase in pregnancy, so cleaning is especially recommended; the second trimester is the best time.

title: Private health insurance, complementary insurance and SGK for dental treatment: a payment guide for Beylikdüzü
desc: Does private health insurance, complementary health insurance or SGK cover dental treatment in Turkey? Dental cover, limits, waiting periods, pre-approval, invoices and reimbursement, and payment planning at a private clinic in Beylikdüzü.
lead: Dental treatment covered by SGK (Turkey's Social Security Institution) is mostly provided at state oral and dental health hospitals and centres; at private clinics, patients usually pay themselves. Private health insurance generally covers dental treatment only if a separate "dental cover" has been added, and only up to the policy limit. Checking your policy before treatment and getting pre-approval from your insurer with a written treatment plan avoids surprises.

sections.html:
Basic dental treatments covered by general health insurance, such as examinations, fillings, extractions and root canal treatment, are mainly provided at Ministry of Health oral and dental hospitals and centres, and at university dental faculties. Conditions such as age and time limits may apply to dentures. Implants and cosmetic treatments are generally not covered.

At private dental clinics, patients usually pay for treatment themselves. Coverage and conditions change from time to time, so we recommend confirming the current rules with SGK or its ALO 170 helpline.

In short

For people who don't want to wait for an appointment at a state facility, or who need treatments that aren't covered, such as implants, zirconia crowns or clear aligners, private clinics with insurance and payment options become the practical choice.

sections.h: Does private health insurance cover dental treatment?

title: Afraid of the dentist? Step-by-step, unhurried treatment in Beylikdüzü
desc: What causes fear of the dentist (dental anxiety), how to plan a first appointment, comfortable anaesthetic, a "stop" signal, short sessions and practical ways to feel calmer. Dent32's calm approach in Beylikdüzü.
lead: Fear of the dentist is very common and often comes from a painful experience in the past. sections.h: Why are people afraid of the dentist?
sections.html:
Dental anxiety affects a large share of adults; for some it becomes a phobia that leads them to avoid appointments altogether. The most common causes are:

  • A painful treatment in childhood or in the past
  • Fear of needles, blood or the sound of the drill
  • Feeling a loss of control and being unable to speak with your mouth open
  • Embarrassment about the state of your teeth and fear of being judged
  • Not knowing how long the treatment will take or what will happen

When fear delays treatment, a small cavity can turn into a root canal and a loose tooth into an extraction. Avoidance creates a cycle that leads to bigger, scarier treatments.

sections.h: How we work with anxious patients at Dent32
sections.html:
• Meet first: At the first appointment we just talk and examine. If you don't feel ready, we don't start treatment that day.
  • Tell, show, do: We explain the instrument we'll use and what you'll feel beforehand, and show it to you if you like.
  • Stop signal: Raise your hand and we stop straight away. This simple rule makes you feel in control.
  • Anaesthetic you barely feel: A numbing gel is applied to the gum first and the anaesthetic is given slowly. We don't start until you're fully numb.
  • Short sessions: We start with short, easy procedures and lengthen sessions as trust builds.
  • No judgement: Not having seen a dentist for a long time isn't something we criticise; it's simply where we start.
In short

Just tell us about your fear when you book. It lets the dentist plan the session around you.

One of our Google reviews sums it up well: "Even people with a fear of dentists like me can go there comfortably. The whole team is friendly and helpful in every situation." (Tülay Ç.)   • Breathe slowly: in through your nose for 4 seconds, out through your mouth for 6.

title: Dental abscess and facial swelling: will it go away on its own, and when is it an emergency?
desc: What is a dental abscess, what are the symptoms, does it go away on its own, are antibiotics enough, when should facial swelling send you to A&E, and how is it treated? Root canal treatment, drainage and extraction.
lead: A dental abscess is a pus-filled infection at the tip of a tooth's root or in the gum, and it doesn't go away on its own. Even if the abscess bursts and the pain eases, it comes back unless the source of the infection is treated. Treatment means draining the abscess and removing the source with root canal treatment, gum treatment or extraction. Fast-growing facial swelling, difficulty swallowing or breathing, and a high fever are emergency signs.

sections.h: What is a dental abscess, and what causes it?
sections.html:
An abscess is a collection of pus that forms when the body walls off a bacterial infection. There are two main types in teeth:

  • Root tip (periapical) abscess: Deep decay or a crack kills the tooth's nerve, and infection spreads from the root tip into the bone.
  • Gum (periodontal) abscess: Develops in the pocket between tooth and gum in advanced gum disease.

An abscess can also develop in teeth that have already had root canal treatment or a crown, if the canals weren't fully cleaned or there is leakage under the crown.

• Throbbing, constant pain that gets worse at night

  • A pimple-like swelling on the gum, sometimes with discharge
  • Swelling in the cheek, jaw or under the eye
  • A bad taste or smell in the mouth
  • Fever, feeling unwell, swollen lymph nodes in the neck

Small bump with discharge on the gum, no painDentist within a few days
In short

Pain suddenly stopping isn't always a good sign. When an abscess bursts and drains, or the nerve dies completely, the pain may ease but the infection continues.

sections.h: Does an abscess go away on its own? Are antibiotics enough?
sections.html: No. Antibiotics can help control spreading infection and fever, but they can't reach the dead nerve tissue or gum pocket at the source. Once the course ends, the abscess often comes back. That's why antibiotics are used alongside treatment when the dentist thinks they're needed, not as treatment on their own. Details: do antibiotics cure toothache?.

1. Examination and X-ray: The source and spread of the abscess are identified.
  2. Drainage: If needed, the pus is drained by opening the tooth or through a small cut in the gum; pain usually eases quickly.
  3. Treating the source: Root canal treatment for the tooth, or deep cleaning and gum treatment for a gum abscess.
  4. A tooth that can't be saved: If the tooth can't be restored, it's extracted and replacing it is planned.
  5. Protection: After root canal treatment, a crown is often recommended so the tooth doesn't fracture.

• Take a painkiller your doctor has previously said is suitable for you, at the dose on the pack.
  • Apply cold to the cheek; avoid heat, which can help the infection spread.
  • Rinse gently with warm salt water.
  • Don't try to burst the gum swelling with a needle or sharp object.
  • Don't start old antibiotics you have at home on your own.

For an abscess or swelling that starts at the weekend in Beylikdüzü, see our on-call and emergency dentist guide, or send a photo to Dent32 on WhatsApp (+90 555 011 33 68) to ask for a same-day assessment.

faq.q: Does a dental abscess go away on its own?
faq.a: No. Even if the abscess drains and the pain eases, it comes back unless the source of the infection is treated.

faq.q: Can an abscessed tooth have root canal treatment?
faq.a: Yes. Most abscessed teeth can be saved with root canal treatment; the pus is drained first if needed.

faq.q: Which antibiotic is used for an abscess?
faq.a: Whether you need an antibiotic, and which one, is decided by the dentist after an examination. Don't start antibiotics on your own.

faq.q: Can a tooth be taken out if my face is swollen?
faq.a: Sometimes the infection needs to be controlled first; sometimes taking the tooth out lets the pus drain. The decision is made at the examination.

faq.q: Is an abscess dangerous?
faq.a: If untreated, the infection can spread into the face and neck. With fast-growing swelling and difficulty breathing, go to A&E.

title: My filling fell out or my crown came off: what should I do, and can I use a pharmacy kit?
desc: What to do first when a filling falls out or a crown comes off: pain, sensitivity, temporary fixes, pharmacy dental cement, whether the crown can be re-cemented and how long you can wait.
lead: If a filling has fallen out or a crown has come off, the first thing to do is keep the piece and see a dentist within a few days. Without pain, it isn't an emergency, but the exposed tooth is vulnerable to decay, fracture and sensitivity. If the crown is intact and the tooth underneath is suitable, it can often be re-cemented in the same visit.

sections.html:
1. If you haven't swallowed it, clean the piece, put it in a container and bring it to your appointment.
  2. Rinse your mouth with warm water.
  3. If a sharp edge is cutting your tongue or cheek, cover it temporarily with orthodontic wax or sugar-free gum.
  4. Don't chew on that side; avoid very hot, very cold and sugary food.
  5. See a dentist within a few days, or the same day if you have sensitivity or pain.
In short

A filling or crown coming loose is often a sign that new decay has started underneath. So the tooth needs checking, not just the piece putting back.

sections.h: Why do fillings and crowns fall out?
sections.html:
• New decay starting at the edge of the filling or crown
  • Biting hard objects (ice, nuts in shells, pens) or sticky sweets
  • Clenching and grinding at night: bruxism and night guards
  • The cement wearing away over time
  • A very large filling weakening the remaining walls of the tooth

sections.h: Can I use a pharmacy dental cement?
sections.html:
Temporary filling materials and crown cements sold in pharmacies are a short-term fix for a few days until you see a dentist. Before refitting a crown, both the crown and the tooth need cleaning, and you must be sure it seats correctly; a crown that sits wrongly upsets your bite and irritates the gum.

Never use household superglue or similar products. They damage tissue, make it harder to re-cement the crown properly and seal in any decay underneath, letting it progress.

SituationLikely treatment
Small filling lost, tooth soundA new white filling, usually in one visit
Large filling lost, tooth walls weakAn inlay, onlay or crown
Crown intact, tooth underneath healthyCleaning and re-cementing in the same visit
Decay under the crownTreating the decay and usually a new crown
Root fractured along with the crownRoot canal treatment and a post, or extraction and an implant assessment

We explain white fillings in dental fillings in Beylikdüzü and crown materials in types of dental crowns.

Without pain or sensitivity, booking within a few days is usually enough. Waiting for weeks, however, can lead to the exposed tooth decaying or fracturing, or the neighbouring teeth shifting. If a crown is left out for a long time, the tooth can move and the old crown may no longer fit.

If you have throbbing pain, swelling or pain that wakes you at night, the nerve may be involved; get seen the same day. Dent32 in Beylikdüzü is open every day, including weekends: +90 555 011 33 68.

faq.q: Can a crown that came off be put back?
faq.a: If the crown is intact and the tooth underneath is healthy, it can often be cleaned and re-cemented in the same visit.

faq.q: My filling fell out but it doesn't hurt. Is it urgent?
faq.a: It isn't an emergency, but you should go within a few days. The exposed tooth is vulnerable to decay and fracture.

faq.q: Can I stick my crown back with superglue?
faq.a: No. Household glues damage tissue and make it harder to re-cement the crown properly.

faq.q: I swallowed my filling. What happens?
faq.a: Small pieces of filling usually pass through the digestive system without problems. If you're coughing or short of breath, see a doctor immediately.

faq.q: My temporary crown fell off. What should I do?
faq.a: Keep the temporary crown and contact the clinic. It's important that the tooth isn't left exposed while the permanent crown is being made.

title: How long do dental implants last? What affects their lifespan, and peri-implantitis
desc: How long does a dental implant last, and is it for life? The lifespan of the implant and its crown, signs of peri-implantitis, the effect of smoking and diabetes, and the care and check-ups that keep implants going.
lead: Well-planned, well-maintained implants last for many years in most patients, often for life; studies report that the large majority (around 90–95%) are still functioning after 10 years. The crown on top may need replacing over time because of wear. The biggest threat to long-term success is peri-implantitis, inflammation around the implant.

sections.h: The implant and the tooth on top don't have the same lifespan
sections.html:
PartWhat to expectWhat shortens it
Implant (the screw in the bone)Once integrated, and with continued care, usually many yearsPeri-implantitis, smoking, uncontrolled diabetes
Abutment and screwLong-lasting; occasional looseningExcessive biting force, clenching
Crown or bridgeMany years depending on material; may be renewed in timeClenching, biting hard objects, fracture
In short

The most honest answer to "how long does an implant last?" is this: the implant itself usually stays for many years; the tooth on top may need maintenance and renewal over time, like any crown.

• Planning: Implants placed at the right length and position using a CT scan transfer forces evenly to the bone.
  • Bone and gum: Enough bone and healthy, thick gum around the implant improve long-term success.
  • Smoking: Impairs integration and healing, and clearly increases the risk of peri-implantitis.
  • Diabetes: Well-controlled diabetes isn't a barrier; poorly controlled blood sugar speeds up inflammation.
  • History of gum disease: People who lost teeth to gum disease get inflammation around implants more often, so regular maintenance matters even more.
  • Clenching: Can lead to fractured crowns and loose screws; a night guard is recommended.
  • A quality system: Choose implant brands with strong clinical evidence and parts that will still be available years later.

sections.h: What is peri-implantitis, and how do you spot it?
sections.html:
Peri-implantitis is plaque-related inflammation of the gum and bone around an implant. It starts with a reversible stage affecting only the gum (peri-implant mucositis); if untreated, the bone supporting the implant begins to break down. Because it's often painless, it can go unnoticed without regular check-ups.

  • Bleeding around the implant when brushing
  • Redness, swelling or discharge from the gum
  • Gum receding around the implant, with metal showing
  • A bad taste or smell
  • Movement of the implant at an advanced stage

At an early stage it can be treated with professional cleaning and better home care; advanced stages may need surgical treatment.

• Brush twice a day with a soft brush and fluoride toothpaste
  • Clean around the implant with an interdental brush, implant floss or a water flosser
  • Have a check-up and professional clean at least once or twice a year; more often if you have a history of gum disease
  • Have the bone level monitored with check-up X-rays at intervals
  • Stop or cut down smoking
  • Wear a night guard if you clench

We explain the first days in dental implant aftercare and the whole process in dental implants in Beylikdüzü.

Implant treatment isn't finished when the crown goes in. Afterwards, we set your check-up intervals and, at each visit, monitor gum health, your bite and, when needed, the bone level on X-rays. You're also welcome to come to us for check-ups on implants placed elsewhere; if you know the brand, mention it when booking.

faq.q: Do dental implants last for life?
faq.a: Most well-planned, well-maintained implants last for many years, often for life. The crown on top may need replacing in time.

faq.q: Can implants decay?
faq.a: Implants don't decay, but the gum and bone around them can become inflamed because of plaque (peri-implantitis).

faq.q: Can the body reject an implant?
faq.a: True titanium allergy is very rare. Implants are usually lost because they fail to integrate or because of peri-implantitis.

faq.q: What should I do if my implant bleeds?
faq.a: Bleeding may be the first sign of inflammation around the implant. It's easier to treat early, so come in for a check.

faq.q: Does smoking affect how long implants last?
faq.a: Yes. Smoking impairs integration and increases the risk of peri-implantitis; stopping helps implants last longer.

title: Why do teeth turn yellow? Coffee, tea, smoking, age and medicines
desc: Why teeth turn yellow: coffee, tea and smoking stains, enamel thinning with age, medicines, root canal treatment and fluorosis. Which discolouration responds to cleaning, whitening, bonding or veneers?
lead: Tooth discolouration comes in two kinds: external stains left on the surface by things like coffee, tea and smoking, and internal discolouration from the structure of the tooth itself. External stains are often largely removed by a scale and polish; internal discolouration needs whitening and, in more severe cases, bonding or veneers. The right solution depends on the cause.

sections.h: External stains: colour on the surface
sections.html:
• Coffee, tea, red wine, cola: Dark pigments cling to the thin film on the enamel surface.
  • Cigarettes and shisha: Tar and nicotine leave stubborn yellow-brown stains.
  • Tartar: Its rough surface picks up colour more easily, especially behind the lower front teeth.
  • Some mouthwashes: Long-term use of chlorhexidine mouthwash can cause brown staining.

Most of these stains are removed by a scale and polish. If your teeth still aren't as light as you'd like afterwards, whitening can be considered.

sections.h: Internal discolouration: colour from the tooth itself
sections.html:
• Age: Over the years, enamel thins and more of the yellower dentine beneath shows through.
  • Genetics: Some people naturally have yellower or greyer teeth.
  • Nerve death and root canal treatment: A tooth whose nerve dies after a knock or decay can turn grey over time; it's the most common reason for a single dark tooth.
  • Medicines: Tetracycline-type antibiotics taken while teeth are forming (in pregnancy and childhood) can cause grey-brown bands.
  • Too much fluoride (fluorosis): Excess fluoride in childhood can cause white or brown spots.
  • Old fillings: Amalgam fillings can give a tooth a grey cast; composite fillings can discolour over time.
In short

One tooth darker than the rest is usually a sign of a problem with the nerve. In that case, the tooth's health should be checked with an X-ray first.

SituationRecommended approach
Coffee, tea or smoking stainsScale and polish; whitening if needed
General yellowing from age or geneticsIn-clinic or at-home tray whitening
A single dark root-treated toothInternal whitening; veneer or zirconia crown if needed
Tetracycline or fluorosis stainingWhitening often isn't enough; bonding or veneers
Discoloured old fillingsReplacing the fillings

We explain whitening options in teeth whitening in Beylikdüzü, and no-drill corrections in dental bonding and laminate veneers. Remember that whitening doesn't change the colour of crowns or fillings.

• Rinse with water after dark drinks, and use a straw where you can.
  • Don't brush straight after acidic drinks; wait 30 minutes while the enamel is softened.
  • Brush twice a day with fluoride toothpaste; don't use whitening toothpastes all the time, as they can be abrasive.
  • Stopping smoking protects both colour and gum health.
  • Have a professional clean every 6–12 months.

At the examination we record your tooth shade with a shade guide, check whether the stains are external or internal and look for any nerve problem. We then suggest the option that gives the best result with the least intervention. To book: +90 555 011 33 68 (WhatsApp and phone). Dent32 is a dental clinic on the E-5 service road in Beylikdüzü, open every day including weekends.

faq.q: Can yellow teeth go back to white?
faq.a: External stains largely come off with cleaning and polishing. The tooth's own colour can be lightened by a few shades with whitening.

faq.q: Do baking soda or lemon whiten teeth?
faq.a: Not recommended. Baking soda can be abrasive, and acids like lemon erode enamel, making teeth look yellower in the long run.

faq.q: Do whitening toothpastes work?
faq.a: They can reduce surface stains but don't noticeably change the tooth's own colour. Constant long-term use can wear enamel.

faq.q: Why has one of my teeth gone dark?
faq.a: The most common reason is the nerve being affected after a knock or deep decay. It needs checking with an X-ray.

faq.q: Will whitening last if I keep drinking coffee?
faq.a: The effect fades sooner. Rinsing with water after coffee and regular cleaning help it last longer.

title: Do antibiotics and painkillers cure toothache? When they're needed and when they're not
desc: Do antibiotics work for toothache? Which toothache needs antibiotics and which doesn't, painkillers, the risks of using leftover antibiotics, and the real treatment for tooth pain.
lead: Most toothache comes from inflammation of the nerve inside the tooth and doesn't respond to antibiotics, because the problem isn't bacteria spreading through the blood but inflamed tissue inside the tooth. Antibiotics are used alongside treatment when the dentist thinks they're needed, in situations that show the infection is spreading, such as facial swelling or fever. The real treatment for the pain is dealing with the source: a filling, root canal treatment or extraction.

sections.h: Why don't antibiotics cure most toothache?
sections.html:
The most common cause of throbbing pain that worsens with cold or heat and wakes you at night is pulpitis: inflammation of the nerve and blood vessels inside the tooth. Because this tissue is enclosed by hard tooth walls, swelling creates pressure and pain. Antibiotics don't relieve that pressure, and they can't reach a nerve whose blood supply is compromised.

Clinical guidance from dental associations also recommends treating the source (the first stage of root canal treatment, drainage or extraction) plus painkillers, rather than antibiotics, for toothache without signs of spreading infection.

In short

When pain eases a few days after starting antibiotics, it's often coincidence or because the nerve has died completely. The problem hasn't gone; it can come back weeks or months later as an abscess.

SituationAntibiotics?
Nerve inflammation (pulpitis), no fever or swellingUsually not; treat the source
Localised abscess that can be drainedDrainage and root canal treatment are often enough
Swelling spreading to the face or neck, fever, feeling unwellYes, alongside treatment; A&E if severe
Limited mouth opening, swollen lymph nodesOften yes, depending on the dentist's assessment
Immunocompromised patients, some heart conditionsPreventive or therapeutic use decided by the dentist

sections.h: Why is using leftover antibiotics risky?
sections.html:
• The wrong drug or dose can suppress and mask the infection, delaying proper treatment.
  • Unnecessary antibiotics carry risks of diarrhoea, stomach upset and allergic reactions.
  • They contribute to bacteria becoming resistant, so the drug may not work when it's really needed.
  • Stopping a course halfway increases the risk of resistance.

Painkillers are the right way to keep pain under control until you see a dentist. Take a painkiller your doctor has previously said is suitable for you, at the dose on the pack; if you have stomach problems, kidney disease, take blood thinners or are pregnant, ask your pharmacist or doctor which one is suitable. Don't put aspirin or a painkiller tablet on the tooth or gum; it burns the tissue.

Pain that even painkillers don't touch suggests the nerve is severely inflamed and needs assessing the same day.

sections.h: The real treatment for the pain
sections.html:
Once the cause is found with an examination and X-ray, treatment usually starts with a relieving procedure in a single visit: removing decay and placing a filling, removing the nerve and starting root canal treatment, draining an abscess or extracting a tooth that can't be saved. After these, the pain usually eases noticeably within hours.

For details, see root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü, dental abscess and night and weekend toothache. If you're in pain in Beylikdüzü, message us on WhatsApp (+90 555 011 33 68) to ask for a same-day assessment.

faq.q: Are antibiotics good for toothache?
faq.a: Most toothache comes from nerve inflammation and doesn't respond to antibiotics. They're used only when infection is spreading, alongside treatment.

faq.q: The pain came back when the antibiotics finished. Why?
faq.a: As long as the source of infection is inside the tooth, the pain and swelling return. Treating the source, such as with a root canal or extraction, is needed.

faq.q: Can root canal treatment be done without antibiotics?
faq.a: Yes. Most root canal treatments don't need antibiotics; the dentist decides whether they're needed.

faq.q: Which painkiller should I take for toothache?
faq.a: Agree a painkiller suited to your general health with your doctor or pharmacist, and don't exceed the dose on the pack.

faq.q: Should I start antibiotics if I have swelling?
faq.a: Don't start them on your own. If the swelling is growing fast or affecting your breathing, go to A&E; otherwise see a dentist the same day.

title: How long do zirconia crowns last? Habits that lengthen and shorten their life
desc: How long does a zirconia crown last, can it break, does it discolour? What determines a zirconia crown's lifespan, clenching, gum recession and decay at the margin, and how to protect crowns for years.
lead: Well-planned, well-maintained zirconia crowns last for many years; clinical studies show that the large majority are trouble-free in the first 5–10 years. Zirconia itself doesn't discolour or decay; what usually decides its lifespan is the tooth underneath, gum health and habits such as clenching.

sections.h: What determines a zirconia crown's lifespan?
sections.html:
FactorEffect
The tooth underneathNew decay under or at the edge of the crown may mean it has to be replaced
Gum healthIf the gum recedes, the crown margin becomes visible and the appearance suffers
Clenching and grindingChipping of the porcelain layer and wear on opposing teeth
Planning and fitCrowns with a poor marginal fit have a higher risk of leakage and decay
Type of zirconiaMonolithic (single-piece) zirconia resists chipping better than zirconia layered with porcelain
CareBrushing, cleaning between teeth and regular check-ups
In short

Zirconia doesn't decay, but the tooth under it can. Crowned teeth need cleaning just as carefully as natural ones.

• Chipping of the porcelain layer: Seen mainly in porcelain-layered crowns and in people who clench. Small chips can be polished; larger ones may need a new crown.
  • Decay at the margin: Starts when plaque collects at the crown edge; caught early, it can be repaired.
  • Gum recession: With age or hard brushing, the crown margin can become exposed.
  • Crown coming off: Cement failure or fracture of the tooth underneath; see what to do if a crown comes off.
  • Sensitivity: Mild sensitivity in the first weeks after fitting is normal: sensitivity after crowns.

• Brush twice a day with a soft brush and fluoride toothpaste, gently cleaning crown margins at the gum line.
  • Clean between crowned teeth with floss, interdental brushes or bridge floss.
  • Don't bite ice, nuts in shells or pens, and don't use your teeth to open bottles or packets.
  • If you clench at night, wear a night guard.
  • Have a check-up and professional clean every 6–12 months.
  • Stopping smoking protects gum health and crown margins.

sections.h: Do zirconia crowns discolour or turn yellow?
sections.html:
Zirconia and its ceramic surface don't change colour, and they're far less affected by coffee and tea than natural teeth. Over time, stains and tartar on the surface can dull them; professional cleaning and polishing remove this. As your natural teeth darken with age, or if they're whitened, a colour difference with your crowns can appear, so whitening should be planned before crowns are made.

You're welcome to come to us for a check of crowns made elsewhere. At the examination we assess the marginal fit, gums and bite and, if needed, check the tooth under the crown with an X-ray. When planning new crowns, we consider minimal tooth reduction, a good marginal fit and any clenching together; see zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü for details.
