faq.q: Do zirconia crowns last for life?
faq.a: A lifetime can't be guaranteed, but well-planned, well-maintained zirconia crowns can be used trouble-free for many years.

faq.q: Can zirconia break?
faq.a: The zirconia framework is very strong; chipping is mostly seen in the porcelain layered on top and in people who clench.

faq.q: Can teeth decay under zirconia?
faq.a: Zirconia doesn't decay, but the tooth underneath can, especially at the crown margin. Regular cleaning and check-ups matter.

faq.q: Do zirconia crowns turn yellow?
faq.a: No. Surface stains can make them look dull; cleaning and polishing remove them.

faq.q: When should old zirconia crowns be replaced?
faq.a: Replacement comes up if there's decay at the margin, marked gum recession, a fracture or a poor fit. The decision is made at the examination.

title: Child's tooth broken or knocked out after a fall: what to do in the first 30 minutes
desc: First aid for a tooth broken or knocked out by a fall, sport or a blow: how to put an adult tooth back, why baby teeth aren't replanted, keeping the tooth in milk, broken fragments and how quickly to see a dentist.
lead: An adult tooth knocked out completely has the best chance of being saved if it's put back within the first 30–60 minutes. Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root; if it's dirty, rinse it for a few seconds in milk or saline and, if you can, put it straight back in its socket. If you can't, keep it in milk and go to a dentist without delay. Baby teeth are not put back.

sections.h: Knocked-out adult tooth: first aid step by step
sections.html:
1. Stay calm and find the tooth. Hold it by the crown (the white part); don't touch the root.
  2. If it's dirty, rinse it in cold milk, saline or tap water for no more than 10 seconds. Don't scrub, wipe or use soap.
  3. If possible, put the tooth straight back into its socket the right way round. Have the person bite on a clean handkerchief or gauze to hold it in place.
  4. If you can't put it back, keep the tooth in a glass of cold milk. If there's no milk, use saline; a conscious adult can also keep it in saliva inside the cheek. Never wrap it in a dry tissue or keep it in water.
  5. Go to a dentist without delay. Time is the most important factor in saving the tooth.
In short

The living cells on the tooth's root die as they dry out. Putting the tooth back or keeping it in milk in the first minutes decides whether it stays in the mouth long term.

sections.h: What if a baby tooth is knocked out?
sections.html:
A knocked-out baby tooth is not put back; doing so can damage the adult tooth developing underneath. Stop the bleeding by pressing with clean gauze and take your child to a dentist the same day. The dentist checks for damage to the adult tooth and surrounding tissues; a space maintainer may be needed to hold the space of a baby tooth lost early.

If you're not sure whether it's a baby or adult tooth, as a general rule the front teeth are mostly baby teeth before the age of 6–7. If in doubt, keep the tooth in milk and see a dentist immediately.

SituationWhat to do
Part of the tooth has broken offFind the fragment and keep it in milk or water; it can often be bonded back. See a dentist the same day
Pink-red spot on the broken surface (nerve exposed)See a dentist the same day, within a few hours if possible
Tooth loosened or pushed out of positionDon't force it; the dentist repositions and splints it the same day
Tooth pushed up into the gumDentist the same day; treatment depends on the type of tooth and age
Cut lip, tongue or gumApply cold and pressure; deep cuts may need stitches

For broken teeth in adults, see what to do if you break a tooth.

sections.h: When to go to A&E first
sections.html:
• Loss of consciousness, vomiting, severe headache or drowsiness (signs of head injury)
  • Bleeding that won't stop
  • A change in the shape of the jaw or difficulty opening and closing the mouth (possible jaw fracture)
  • Difficulty breathing, or suspicion that the tooth was swallowed or inhaled

With any of these signs, go to A&E first; dental treatment follows once the person's general condition has been assessed.

Injured teeth can change colour or the nerve can be affected even months later, so it's important to attend the follow-up appointments the dentist recommends (usually after a few weeks, a few months and a year). Replanted teeth are splinted to the neighbouring teeth with a flexible wire for a few weeks.

A custom mouthguard protects the teeth during basketball, football, combat sports and cycling. We cover preventive care for children in children's dentist in Beylikdüzü. We're open at weekends in Beylikdüzü too; after an injury, contact us straight away by WhatsApp or phone: +90 555 011 33 68.

faq.q: Can a knocked-out tooth be put back?
faq.a: Adult teeth often survive, especially if put back within the first 30–60 minutes. Baby teeth are not put back.

faq.q: What should I keep a knocked-out tooth in?
faq.a: Cold milk is best. If there's no milk, saline can be used. Don't keep it in water or a dry tissue.

faq.q: Can a broken piece of tooth be stuck back on?
faq.a: Often yes. Keep the fragment in milk or water and bring it to a dentist the same day.

faq.q: The tooth went grey after a knock. What does it mean?
faq.a: It may mean the nerve has been affected. It needs checking with an X-ray, and root canal treatment may be planned if needed.

faq.q: A baby tooth was knocked out. Does anything need to replace it?
faq.a: The dentist checks the adult tooth; a space maintainer may be needed after early loss.

title: What causes bad breath and how do you get rid of it for good?
desc: The most common causes of bad breath (halitosis): tongue coating, gum disease, decay, dry mouth and tonsil stones. What you can do at home, whether mouthwash helps and when to see a dentist.
lead: Most persistent bad breath (around 80–90% of cases) starts in the mouth. The usual culprits are the bacterial coating on the back of the tongue, gum disease and food trapped between the teeth. That is why the fix is rarely mouthwash; it is tongue cleaning, cleaning between the teeth and, where needed, a professional clean and gum treatment.

sections.html:
Bacteria in the mouth break down food debris, shed cells and proteins in gum pockets, releasing volatile sulphur compounds. These gases are the main source of the smell. Bacteria thrive on the back of the tongue, between the teeth, in deepened gum pockets and in decayed cavities.

CauseHow to spot it
Coating on the tongueWhite-yellow layer on the back of the tongue
Gum inflammation and gum diseaseBleeding when brushing, swelling, receding gums
Decay, broken fillings or crown marginsFood trapping, smell from one area
Dry mouthDrinking too little, mouth breathing, some medicines (antidepressants, blood pressure and allergy drugs)
Uncleaned dentures or alignersSmell is stronger when the appliance is removed
Food, drink and smokingGarlic, onion, coffee, alcohol; temporary smell

sections.h: What causes bad breath outside the mouth?
sections.html:
Less often, bad breath comes from elsewhere. Tonsil stones and chronic tonsillitis, sinusitis and post-nasal drip, and acid reflux are the most common. Uncontrolled diabetes can give the breath an acetone-like smell, and kidney or liver disease can cause other distinctive odours.

If the dental examination finds no cause in the mouth, we refer you to an ear, nose and throat specialist or your GP.

sections.h: How can I tell if my breath smells?
sections.html:
We get used to our own breath, so it is hard to notice. These simple checks give you an idea:

  • Lick your wrist, let it dry for a few seconds and smell it.
  • Smell a piece of floss after passing it between your back teeth.
  • Gently scrape the back of your tongue with a spoon and smell it.
  • Ask someone you trust.
Morning breath is normal

Saliva flow drops during sleep, so everyone has some morning breath; it goes after breakfast and brushing. Breath that smells all day usually has a cause.

sections.h: What can you do at home?
sections.html:
• Brush twice a day for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Here is the right technique.
  • Scrape your tongue from back to front a few times with a tongue cleaner; this usually makes the quickest difference.
  • Clean between your teeth once a day with floss or interdental brushes.
  • Drink enough water; sugar-free gum increases saliva flow.
  • Take out removable dentures or aligners at night and clean them daily.
  • Stopping smoking reduces both the smell and the risk of gum disease.

Mints and scented mouthwashes only mask the smell for a short time. Alcohol-free mouthwashes containing cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) or zinc can help by lowering the bacterial load. Chlorhexidine mouthwash is effective, but long-term use can stain teeth and change taste, so use it briefly and only on your dentist's advice.

sections.h: What happens at the dental examination?
sections.html:
We check the teeth, tongue, gums and any appliances, measure gum pockets and take X-rays if needed. Treatment depends on the source:

  • Professional cleaning and polishing
  • Deep cleaning and gum treatment for gum disease
  • Treating decay and replacing old fillings or crowns with leaking margins
  • Treating inflammation around a partly erupted wisdom tooth, or removing it if needed

Dent32 in Beylikdüzü sees patients seven days a week. If bad breath has lasted several weeks, book an examination.

faq.q: Is morning breath normal?
faq.a: Yes. Saliva flow drops at night, so everyone has some morning breath. It goes after breakfast and brushing.

faq.q: Does bad breath come from the stomach?
faq.a: Rarely. Reflux can contribute, but most persistent bad breath starts in the mouth. A dental examination is the best first step.

faq.q: Will a professional clean get rid of bad breath?
faq.a: If the smell comes from tartar and gum inflammation, it helps a great deal. For a lasting result you also need tongue cleaning and cleaning between the teeth at home.

faq.q: Why do children get bad breath?
faq.a: Mouth breathing, enlarged adenoids or tonsils, decayed teeth and poor brushing are the most common causes. A dental check and, if needed, a paediatric ENT review are recommended.

title: Dental treatment during pregnancy: what is safe and when is the best time?
desc: Can you have fillings, root canal treatment, extractions, X-rays and local anaesthetic while pregnant? The best trimester, treatments to postpone, pregnancy gingivitis and medicines.
lead: Dental treatment is possible during pregnancy and often should not be postponed. Fillings, root canal treatment, professional cleaning and, if needed, extractions can be done with the right precautions. The most comfortable time is usually the second trimester (roughly months 4 to 6). Whitening, implants and cosmetic treatment are left until after the birth.

sections.h: Why shouldn't dental treatment wait during pregnancy?
sections.html:
Untreated decay or a dental infection gets worse over time, bringing pain, poor sleep, difficulty eating and a greater need for medicines. That is a bigger burden for both mother and baby than a short, planned treatment.

Hormonal changes in pregnancy make the gums more prone to inflammation. Some studies have linked advanced gum disease with premature birth, though cause and effect have not been proven; healthy gums matter either way.

In short

Always tell us you are pregnant. The treatment plan is based on how many weeks pregnant you are and on your obstetrician's advice.

sections.h: Which treatments suit which stage of pregnancy?
sections.html:
StageSuitable treatmentNote
1st trimester (weeks 0–13)Examination, cleaning, urgent care for pain or infectionPlanned treatment is moved to the second trimester where possible, as the baby's organs are forming
2nd trimester (weeks 14–27)Fillings, root canal treatment, extractions, gum treatmentThe best time; nausea eases and sitting in the chair is comfortable
3rd trimester (week 28 onwards)Urgent and short proceduresLong appointments are avoided; a slight left-side tilt is used when lying back

sections.h: Are local anaesthetic and dental X-rays safe for the baby?
sections.html:
The local anaesthetics used in dentistry (lidocaine, articaine) are considered safe in pregnancy at standard doses. Being treated in pain and under stress is worse than being treated with anaesthetic.

Dental X-rays use a very low dose and the beam is aimed only at the mouth. Even so, during pregnancy they are taken only when genuinely needed for diagnosis, with a lead apron and thyroid collar.

sections.h: Which painkillers and antibiotics can be used in pregnancy?
sections.html:
Do not take any medicine on your own while pregnant. Your dentist coordinates prescriptions with your obstetrician. The general approach is:

  • Paracetamol is usually the first choice for pain.
  • Non-steroidal painkillers such as ibuprofen are not recommended, particularly in the second half of pregnancy.
  • When an antibiotic is needed, the penicillin group (for example amoxicillin) is widely used; tetracyclines are not.

Many pregnant women notice red, swollen gums that bleed when brushing. This is pregnancy gingivitis. It is controlled with regular brushing, cleaning between the teeth and, if needed, a professional clean during pregnancy.

Sometimes a small red swelling that bleeds easily (pregnancy epulis) develops on the gum. Most shrink after the birth; if it gets in the way of eating or bleeds often, your dentist will assess it.

Do not brush straight after vomiting, as acid softens the enamel. Rinse with water, or with a teaspoon of baking soda in a glass of water, and brush about half an hour later.

sections.h: Which treatments are left until after the birth?
sections.html:
• Teeth whitening
  • Planned surgery such as implants, bone grafts and sinus lifts
  • Cosmetic treatment such as veneers and zirconia crowns
  • Starting new orthodontic treatment (ongoing treatment usually continues)

Most dental treatment is fine while breastfeeding; local anaesthetic does not interfere with it. A check-up before pregnancy or early on keeps surprises to a minimum.

faq.q: Can I have a tooth extracted while pregnant?
faq.a: Yes, if needed. Planned extractions are best done in the second trimester; pain and infection are treated at any stage.

faq.q: Can I have a filling during pregnancy?
faq.a: Yes. A filling done before decay progresses prevents the need for root canal treatment later. White (composite) fillings are usually preferred.

faq.q: Can I have dental treatment while breastfeeding?
faq.a: Yes. Local anaesthetic and most dental treatment do not interfere with breastfeeding, and any medicines are chosen to suit it.

faq.q: Does the baby take calcium from the mother's teeth?
faq.a: No. The idea that you "lose a tooth for every child" is a myth. More decay in pregnancy is linked to frequent snacking, vomiting and harder-to-keep-up oral care.

title: After a tooth extraction: bleeding, pain, when to eat and dry socket
desc: The first 24 hours after a tooth extraction: how long to bite on the gauze, when to eat, smoking, rinsing, swelling and pain. Signs of dry socket and when to call your dentist.
lead: The most important rule after an extraction is to protect the blood clot that forms in the socket. Biting on the gauze for 30–45 minutes, not spitting, rinsing or using a straw for the first 24 hours, and not smoking for at least 2–3 days do most of the work of healing.

sections.h: What should you do in the first hours after an extraction?
sections.html:
1. Bite firmly on the gauze pad your dentist placed for 30–45 minutes, then remove it.
  2. For the first 24 hours, do not spit, rinse or drink through a straw; these can dislodge the clot.
  3. Hold something cold against your cheek on the extraction side for 15–20 minutes at a time, several times on the first day.
  4. Taking the painkiller your dentist recommends before the numbness wears off makes pain easier to control.
  5. Sleep with your head raised on an extra pillow.
  6. Do not smoke for at least 48–72 hours.
In short

The clot in the socket is the wound's natural dressing. Everything you do in the first days is about protecting it.

sections.h: When can you eat after a tooth extraction?
sections.html:
You can eat once the numbness has gone (usually 2–3 hours). Eating while numb makes it easy to bite your lip or cheek without noticing.

WhenRecommendedAvoid
First dayLukewarm or cold soft food: yoghurt, lukewarm soup, mash, puddingsHot drinks, alcohol, fizzy drinks, straws
Days 2–3Pasta, eggs, cooked vegetables; chew on the other sideNuts, seeds, hard and spicy food
After a weekGradual return to a normal dietWatch for food getting stuck in the socket

sections.h: How long do bleeding, swelling and bruising last?
sections.html:
Pink-tinged saliva is normal for the first 24 hours. If there is active bleeding, place a fresh gauze pad or a moistened black tea bag over the area and bite firmly for 30 minutes; the tannin in tea helps stop bleeding.

Swelling usually peaks on day 2 or 3 and then settles. After the first 24 hours, warm compresses are more soothing than cold. Bruising can appear after difficult or surgical extractions and fades within a week.

sections.h: How should you brush after an extraction?
sections.html:
• Brush your teeth on the first evening, but avoid the extraction site.
  • After 24 hours, gently bathe the area with warm salt water (half a teaspoon of salt in a glass of water) after meals, letting it sit rather than swishing hard.
  • Stitches, if used, are removed after 7–10 days or dissolve on their own.
  • Avoid heavy exercise for 24–48 hours.

sections.h: What is dry socket and how do you recognise it?
sections.html:
Dry socket happens when the clot breaks down early and the bone in the socket is exposed. The typical sign is throbbing pain that gets worse, rather than better, 2–4 days after the extraction and spreads towards the ear. There may be a bad taste or smell and the socket looks empty.

It is more common in smokers, after lower wisdom tooth removal and after difficult extractions. Treatment is simple: your dentist cleans the socket and places a soothing dressing, and the pain usually eases markedly within a few days. Do not just wait it out; contact your dentist.

sections.h: When should you contact your dentist?
sections.html:
• Bleeding that continues for more than an hour despite pressure
  • Swelling that increases after day 3, or a fever
  • Difficulty swallowing or breathing (an emergency)
  • Numbness of the lip, chin or tongue lasting more than 24 hours
  • Signs of dry socket

For problems that start at night or at the weekend, see our emergency toothache guide. We cover what to do about the gap in implant or bridge?; if the gap is left for a long time, the jawbone gradually shrinks.

faq.q: When can I smoke after a tooth extraction?
faq.a: Wait at least 48–72 hours, ideally a week. Smoking can break down the clot and cause dry socket.

faq.q: How long do I need to rest after an extraction?
faq.a: After a simple extraction most people go back to work or school the next day. After surgical wisdom tooth removal, 2–3 days of rest may be needed.

faq.q: Can I drink hot tea after an extraction?
faq.a: Avoid hot drinks on the first day, as they can increase bleeding. Lukewarm drinks are fine.

faq.q: Can an implant be placed straight after an extraction?
faq.a: In suitable cases, yes, in the same appointment. More often we wait a few weeks to a few months, depending on the bone and any infection.

title: Sensitive teeth to cold and heat: causes, home care and treatment
desc: Why are teeth sensitive, does sensitive toothpaste work, and when should you suspect decay or nerve inflammation? Treatment options including fluoride varnish, bonding, gum treatment and night guards.
lead: A sharp twinge with cold, heat, sweet or sour food that passes in a few seconds is most often caused by exposed dentine, after enamel wear or gum recession. Sensitive toothpaste brings clear relief for most people within 2–4 weeks. If the pain lingers, starts on its own or wakes you at night, you need an examination to check for decay or nerve inflammation.

sections.html:
Enamel on the crown, and the tissue covering the root, protect the dentine underneath. Dentine contains tiny channels that lead to the nerve, so when it is exposed, cold or sweet stimuli reach the nerve easily.

  • A hard toothbrush and scrubbing sideways with pressure
  • Gum recession exposing the root surface
  • Enamel erosion from acidic drinks, frequent fruit juice or reflux
  • Clenching and grinding
  • A cracked tooth, decay or a leaking filling
  • Temporary sensitivity after whitening, cleaning or crowns

How the pain starts and how long it lasts are important clues:

What the pain is likeLikely cause
A sharp twinge with cold or sweet that passes in secondsExposed dentine (dentine hypersensitivity)
Pain lasting more than 30 seconds after the trigger is goneEarly inflammation of the nerve
Spontaneous, throbbing pain that wakes you at nightAdvanced nerve inflammation; root canal treatment may be needed
Sudden pain when biting down and releasingA cracked tooth or a high filling

sections.h: What helps sensitive teeth at home?
sections.html:
• Use a sensitive toothpaste containing potassium nitrate, stannous fluoride or arginine twice a day; spit after brushing but do not rinse.
  • At night you can dab a thin layer of the toothpaste onto the sensitive area with your finger.
  • Switch to a soft brush and stop scrubbing sideways with force.
  • Have acidic drinks with meals, and rinse with water afterwards rather than brushing straight away.
  • Avoid abrasive whitening and charcoal toothpastes.
How long to wait?

With regular use, sensitive toothpaste usually works within 2–4 weeks. Sensitivity that does not improve, or that is focused on one tooth, needs an examination.

sections.h: What treatments are available at the clinic?
sections.html:
• Fluoride varnish or special agents that seal the dentine channels
  • Covering an exposed root surface with a white filling or bonding
  • Gum treatment for advanced recession and, in suitable cases, a gum graft
  • A night guard if you clench or grind
  • Replacing decayed or failing fillings
  • Root canal treatment as a last resort for severe sensitivity that does not respond to anything else

Sensitivity lasting a few days after whitening is common and settles on its own. We explain how long sensitivity after a crown is normal in sensitivity after dental crowns.

At Dent32 in Beylikdüzü we find the cause of sensitivity through examination and, if needed, X-rays. If your symptoms have lasted several weeks, book an examination.

faq.q: How long does sensitive toothpaste take to work?
faq.a: Usually 2–4 weeks with regular use. Sensitivity may come back if you stop using it.

faq.q: Does tooth sensitivity go away on its own?
faq.a: Sensitivity after whitening or cleaning passes in a few days. If a root surface is exposed or enamel is worn, it is unlikely to disappear for good unless the cause is treated.

faq.q: Can a professional clean cause sensitivity?
faq.a: Mild sensitivity for a few days after cleaning is possible, as surfaces previously covered by tartar are exposed. It eases quickly.

faq.q: What does sensitivity in one tooth mean?
faq.a: Sensitivity limited to one tooth usually points to decay, a crack or a problem with a filling, and needs an examination.

title: Broken or cracked tooth: what to do straight away and how it is treated
desc: A chipped front tooth, a cracked tooth or a tooth knocked out: first aid, how to store the broken piece, which situations are urgent, and bonding, crowns or root canal treatment depending on the break.
lead: If you break a tooth, rinse your mouth with warm water, keep the broken piece in milk or water if you can find it, and see a dentist the same day. If the whole tooth has been knocked out, it is an emergency: putting it back in the socket without touching the root, or keeping it in milk and reaching a dentist within the first hour, greatly improves the chance of saving it.

sections.h: What should you do the moment a tooth breaks?
sections.html:
1. Rinse your mouth gently with warm water.
  2. If there is bleeding, press a clean gauze pad or tissue on it for 10 minutes.
  3. Find the broken piece and keep it in a container of milk or water so it does not dry out.
  4. Hold something cold against your cheek to limit swelling.
  5. If a sharp edge is cutting your tongue or cheek, cover it with sugar-free gum or dental wax from a pharmacy.
  6. Do not chew on that side, avoid hot and cold, and see a dentist the same day.
In short

Even if a broken tooth does not hurt, enamel cannot repair itself. A small repair done early can prevent the need for root canal treatment or a crown later.

sections.h: What if the whole tooth is knocked out?
sections.html:
A permanent tooth knocked completely out of its socket (avulsion) is one of the true dental emergencies; minutes matter.

  • Hold the tooth by the crown (the part you normally see), not the root.
  • If it is dirty, rinse it for a few seconds in milk or water; do not scrub or dry it.
  • If you can, push it back into the socket and bite on a clean tissue to hold it in place.
  • If not, carry it in a glass of milk or, for adults, inside the cheek in saliva.
  • Get to a dentist without delay, ideally within the first hour.

Baby teeth are not put back, as this can damage the permanent tooth underneath. The child still needs to be seen the same day.

sections.h: How is each type of break treated?
sections.html:
Type of breakSignsTreatment
Fine crack lines in the enamelUsually noneUsually no treatment; monitoring
Small chipped corner or edgeRough edge, mild sensitivityBonding or a white filling; the fragment can sometimes be reattached
Large break not reaching the nerveCold sensitivity, obvious loss of toothLarger filling, onlay or crown
Break reaching the nervePink-red dot, severe pain or bleedingRoot canal treatment followed by a crown
Cracked toothSudden pain when biting and releasingA crown to stop the crack spreading; root canal treatment if needed
Vertical root fracturePain on biting, recurring swellingUsually extraction and an implant or bridge

sections.h: How do you know if a tooth is cracked?
sections.html:
Cracked teeth often cannot be seen by eye or on an X-ray. The classic sign is a short, sharp pain when biting on something hard or when releasing the bite; cold sensitivity may come with it. Cracks are more common in teeth with large fillings and in people who clench.

A crack found early can usually be protected with a crown that holds the tooth together. Once it extends into the root, saving the tooth becomes much harder.

sections.h: How can you prevent broken teeth?
sections.html:
• Do not bite ice, seeds, pens or nails, and do not open packets or bottles with your teeth.
  • Wear a mouthguard for contact sports.
  • If you clench, wear a night guard.
  • Ask your dentist whether back teeth with very large fillings or root canal treatment should be protected with a crown.

Dent32 in Beylikdüzü is open seven days a week; for teeth broken at the weekend, see our weekend appointments.

faq.q: Is a broken tooth an emergency?
faq.a: See a dentist the same day if the tooth has been knocked out, if there is bleeding or severe pain, or if you can see a pink-red dot in the break. Small painless chips can be repaired within a few days.

faq.q: Can the broken piece be stuck back on?
faq.a: If the piece is large, intact and was kept moist, it can often be bonded back in place.

faq.q: Does a broken tooth heal on its own?
faq.a: No. Enamel and dentine cannot repair themselves; an untreated break can grow and decay over time.

faq.q: My child's baby tooth broke. What should I do?
faq.a: Have it seen the same day. A baby tooth that has been knocked out is not put back, but the permanent tooth underneath needs to be checked.

title: How to brush your teeth properly: toothpaste, floss and interdental brushes
desc: How often and for how long should you brush, which toothpaste and brush to choose, and is an electric toothbrush better? Floss, interdental brushes, water flossers and tongue cleaning step by step.
lead: Brushing twice a day for at least two minutes with fluoride toothpaste and a soft brush is enough; technique is what makes the difference. Angling the brush at 45 degrees to the gum line and using small movements, spitting out the toothpaste without rinsing, and cleaning between your teeth once a day with floss or interdental brushes clearly lowers the risk of decay and gum disease.

sections.html:
1. Put a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste on the brush.
  2. Place the bristles at a 45-degree angle where the teeth meet the gums.
  3. Use small back-and-forth or circular movements over two or three teeth at a time, without pressing hard.
  4. Clean the outer, inner and biting surfaces in turn; hold the brush upright for the inside of the front teeth.
  5. Spend at least two minutes in total; you can split your mouth into four areas and give each 30 seconds.
  6. Spit out the toothpaste but do not rinse with water, so the fluoride stays on the teeth.
In short

Scrubbing hard from side to side causes gum recession and wears enamel. More force does not mean a better clean.

Fluoride is the most important ingredient. The recommended amount by age is:

AgeAmountFluoride
0–3 yearsA thin smear, the size of a grain of riceAt least 1000 ppm
3–6 yearsPea-sized1000–1450 ppm
7 years and adultsPea-sized1350–1500 ppm

If you have sensitivity, a sensitive toothpaste can help. Some whitening and charcoal toothpastes are abrasive, so they are not recommended for long-term use on their own.

Both work well with good technique. Rechargeable brushes with oscillating-rotating heads give a small advantage in plaque removal, and models with a pressure sensor stop you pressing too hard. Whichever you choose:

  • Use soft or medium-soft bristles.
  • Replace the brush or head about every three months, or sooner if the bristles splay.
  • Replace your brush after a cold, flu or throat infection.

sections.h: Floss, interdental brushes or a water flosser?
sections.html:
A toothbrush cannot reach between the teeth, where decay and gum disease most often start. That is why you need to clean between your teeth once a day.

ToolBest for
FlossTight contacts between teeth, no gum recession
Interdental brushesWider gaps, gum recession, bridges and implants
Water flosserExtra cleaning with braces, implants and bridges; not a replacement for floss

If your gums bleed when you brush, do not stop; bleeding usually means inflammation and settles within 1–2 weeks of regular care. If it does not, read our guide to bleeding gums.

sections.h: Do you need tongue cleaning and mouthwash?
sections.html:
The coating on the back of the tongue is the most common cause of bad breath. Scraping it from back to front once a day with a tongue cleaner is enough.

Mouthwash is optional. If you use one, use it at a different time of day rather than straight after brushing, so it does not wash away the fluoride.

• The most important brush is the one before bed, as saliva flow drops during sleep and decay risk rises.
  • The second brush can be in the morning, before or after breakfast.
  • Wait 30–60 minutes after acidic food and drinks such as fruit juice, fizzy drinks and vinegar.
  • If you have braces, implants or a bridge, ask your dentist about cleaning aids suited to you.

A check-up once or twice a year and a professional clean when needed take care of the areas you cannot reach at home.

faq.q: Is it bad to brush straight after eating?
faq.a: Not after an ordinary meal. After acidic food or drinks, wait 30–60 minutes, as enamel is temporarily softened.

faq.q: My gums bleed when I brush. Should I stop?
faq.a: No. Bleeding is usually plaque-related inflammation and improves with gentle, regular brushing. If it does not settle in 1–2 weeks, see a dentist.

faq.q: Does flossing widen the gaps between teeth?
faq.a: No. Correct flossing does not open up gaps; as bleeding and swelling settle, the gums firm up.

faq.q: Until what age should children have help brushing?
faq.a: Parents are usually advised to help with brushing, or check it afterwards, until about age 7–8.

title: Orthodontics for adults: is there an age limit for braces or clear aligners?
desc: Is there an upper age limit for orthodontic treatment? Orthodontics in your 30s, 40s and 50s, clear aligners and braces, treatment time, and what to consider with gum disease or missing teeth.
lead: There is no upper age limit for orthodontic treatment; as long as the bone and gums supporting the teeth are healthy, teeth can be moved safely in your 30s, 40s and 50s. Adult treatment usually takes 12–24 months, clear aligners are a popular choice, and any gum disease must be brought under control first.

sections.h: Can teeth still be moved in adulthood?
sections.html:
Yes. The bone around the teeth renews itself throughout life, and orthodontics uses this natural renewal to move teeth slowly. Movement may be a little slower in adults, but results are as good as in children.

The main difference is that jaw growth has finished. Skeletal problems that can be guided in childhood may, in severe adult cases, need jaw surgery alongside orthodontics.

In short

Gum and bone health matter, not age. In a healthy mouth, orthodontics is possible after 50 too.

sections.h: Why do adults have orthodontic treatment?
sections.html:
• Crowded teeth are harder to clean, raising the risk of decay and gum disease.
  • A poor bite can cause heavy wear and fractures on some teeth.
  • Teeth straightened in childhood can crowd again over the years if retainers were not worn.
  • A gap may need to be opened or closed before an implant or bridge.
  • Aligning teeth before veneers means less tooth needs to be removed.
  • Simply not liking how your smile looks is a valid reason too.

sections.h: What orthodontic options are there for adults?
sections.html:
OptionAdvantageKeep in mind
Clear alignersAlmost invisible, removable, easy to cleanMust be worn about 22 hours a day
Ceramic (clear) bracesLess noticeable than metal, effective in all casesFixed; cleaning between teeth needs care
Metal bracesThe most flexible option for complex casesMore visible

For a detailed comparison, see clear aligners or braces?.

sections.h: How long does adult orthodontic treatment take?
sections.html: Mild crowding can be corrected in 6–12 months. Moderate to severe bite problems usually take 18–24 months, sometimes longer. With aligners, the time depends directly on how many hours a day you wear them. Check-ups are usually every 6–10 weeks.

sections.h: What needs extra care in adult treatment?
sections.html:
• Any gum disease is treated first with gum treatment; teeth are not moved in inflamed gums.
  • Teeth with bone loss are moved with lighter forces and checked more often.
  • Implants do not move; if an implant is planned, its timing is set around the orthodontic plan.
  • Aligner attachments and brackets are planned accordingly on crowned or heavily filled teeth.
  • Root health is checked with X-rays during treatment when needed.

At the end of treatment, retainers stop the teeth drifting back. Adults are usually advised to keep wearing retainers at night for the long term, often for life. See our guide to retainers after orthodontic treatment.

At Dent32, orthodontic treatment is planned by our founding dentist Dr Hüseyin Aşçı. Read our guide to orthodontics in Beylikdüzü or book an examination.

faq.q: Can I get braces after 40?
faq.a: Yes. If your gums and bone are healthy, orthodontic treatment is possible in your 40s, 50s and beyond.

faq.q: Is orthodontic treatment more painful for adults?
faq.a: Not noticeably. There is some pressure for a few days after braces are fitted or a new aligner is started, and it passes quickly.

faq.q: Can I have orthodontics if I have implants?
faq.a: Yes. The implant will not move, but the other teeth can. If the implant has not been placed yet, it is usually better to place it after orthodontics.

faq.q: Are clear aligners suitable for every case?
faq.a: Most crowding and gaps can be treated with aligners. For some complex bite problems, fixed braces give a more predictable result.

title: Retainers after braces or clear aligners: how long do you need to wear them?
desc: Why do teeth move back after orthodontic treatment? Fixed (bonded) and removable retainers compared, how long and how many hours a day to wear them, and what to do if a retainer breaks or is lost.
lead: When orthodontic treatment ends, the teeth have not yet fully settled in their new positions; without retainers they can drift back, especially in the first months. That is why most patients get a thin fixed wire behind the front teeth, a clear retainer worn at night, or both. The safest way to keep the result in the long term is to keep wearing a retainer for life, at least at night.

sections.h: Why do teeth move back after orthodontics?
sections.html:
Teeth are attached to the bone by elastic fibres. During treatment these fibres and the surrounding bone reorganise, and adapting to the new position takes months, or over a year for some fibres in the gum. Teeth that have been rotated are especially prone to turning back.

Even in people who never had orthodontics, teeth, especially the lower front teeth, tend to crowd naturally with age. A retainer protects against this change too.

In short

Retainers are part of treatment, not an optional extra. A retainer worn regularly is the cheapest way to protect your result.

TypeAdvantageDisadvantage
Fixed bonded wire (behind the front teeth)Invisible; nothing to rememberCleaning between teeth needs care; a broken bond may go unnoticed
Clear removable retainerInvisible, easy to clean; covers all teethNeeds discipline to wear; wears or cracks over time
Wire-and-acrylic removable retainerDurable and adjustableMore noticeable when speaking; wire is visible

Your dentist chooses the type or combination based on how crowded the teeth were, your gum health and your habits.

sections.h: How long and how many hours a day should you wear a retainer?
sections.html:
Protocols vary by dentist and case, but a typical approach is:

  • First 3–6 months after treatment: almost all day, except when eating and brushing
  • After that: at night only
  • Long term: for most patients for life, at least a few nights a week
  • Fixed wire: can stay in place for years unless your dentist advises otherwise

sections.h: How do you look after a retainer?
sections.html:
• Clean the retainer every morning with cold or lukewarm water and a soft brush; hot water warps it.
  • Toothpaste can scratch the surface; use liquid soap or the cleaner your dentist recommends.
  • Always keep it in its case when not wearing it; retainers wrapped in a napkin are the ones most often lost.
  • Keep it away from pets.
  • For a fixed wire, use a floss threader or interdental brushes, and have regular professional cleans to stop tartar building up.

sections.h: What if a retainer breaks, is lost or feels tight?
sections.html:
If your retainer is lost or cracked, get a new one without delay; even a few weeks without it can let teeth move. If it feels tight after a few days without it, the teeth have started to shift; if you can still put it in without forcing it, wear it continuously and let your dentist know.

If one end of a fixed wire comes loose or detaches from a tooth, have it repaired within a week. Retention check-ups are usually every 6–12 months.

For the treatment itself, see orthodontics for adults. If your retainer is broken or lost, or you have noticed your teeth shifting, book an examination at Dent32 in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: What happens if I don't wear my retainer?
faq.a: Teeth can drift back towards their old positions, especially in the first months. Significant movement may need orthodontic treatment again.

faq.q: When is a fixed retainer removed?
faq.a: There is no set time; it can stay for years as long as it can be kept clean. If it is removed, a removable retainer is worn at night instead.

faq.q: Can I eat with my retainer in?
faq.a: Removable retainers come out for meals and hot drinks. It is best to take them out when drinking anything other than water.

title: Gummy smile: causes and gum contouring options
desc: Why does too much gum show when you smile? Gum contouring (gingivectomy), crown lengthening, Botox, orthodontics and jaw surgery; healing time and how it fits with smile design.
lead: A smile that shows more than about 3–4 millimetres of gum is called a gummy smile. It is usually caused by gum covering more of the tooth than it should, an upper lip that lifts too high, or excess vertical growth of the upper jaw, and treatment depends on the cause. Where gum covers too much of the tooth, gum contouring is a short procedure done under local anaesthetic.

sections.h: What is a gummy smile and when is it a problem?
sections.html:
Showing 1–2 millimetres of gum above the upper teeth in a broad smile is considered natural. Beyond 3–4 millimetres, the smile starts to look "gummy". Teeth that look short and square, or gum levels that differ between left and right, are other common concerns.

It is not a disease but an aesthetic preference. Treatment is planned when someone is unhappy with their smile.

In short

The right treatment depends on the cause. Gum-related cases are corrected with gum contouring; lip- or jaw-related cases need different approaches.

1. At the examination, gum thickness and pocket depth are measured and the bone level is checked on an X-ray.
  2. The new gum line is planned to suit the whole smile, and can be previewed with photos and a mock-up if needed.
  3. The procedure is done under local anaesthetic and usually takes 30–60 minutes.
  4. If bone reshaping is needed (crown lengthening), it is planned as minor surgery and stitches may be used.

The technique is chosen by the dentist according to the gum and bone.

• The first few days are mildly tender; painkillers keep it comfortable.
  • Soft, lukewarm food is best during this time, and the area is cleaned gently.
  • Surface healing takes 1–2 weeks.
  • The gum line takes a few weeks to reach its final shape; if crowns or veneers are planned, impressions are taken after this.

sections.h: Planning with smile design and veneers
sections.html:
Gum levels frame the smile. If smile design or veneers are planned, adjusting the gums first gives a more harmonious and lasting result. Teeth that look short can sometimes be lengthened with gum contouring alone, without any crowns.

At Dent32 in Beylikdüzü we identify the cause of a gummy smile with an examination and photo analysis, then explain the options that suit you. To be assessed, book an examination.

faq.q: Is gum contouring permanent?
faq.a: When the cause is excess gum, the result is usually permanent. If the bone is also too close to the crown and only gum is removed, the gum can partly grow back, which is why an accurate diagnosis matters.

faq.q: Does gum contouring hurt?
faq.a: It is done under local anaesthetic, so you do not feel pain. There may be mild tenderness for a few days afterwards.

faq.q: Is Botox a permanent fix for a gummy smile?
faq.a: No. Its effect usually lasts 3–6 months and needs repeating. It only works when the cause is an overactive upper lip.

faq.q: Can gum overgrowth be a sign of disease?
faq.a: Yes. Plaque-related inflammation and some blood pressure, epilepsy or immune-suppressing medicines can cause gum overgrowth. In that case the cause is treated first.

title: How do you know if you have tooth decay? Signs, stages and treatment at each stage
desc: Early signs of tooth decay, the stages from white spot to abscess, whether decay can stop on its own, and when you need a filling or root canal treatment. Decay between teeth, X-rays and prevention.
lead: Tooth decay does not hurt at first: the earliest sign is a chalky white spot on the enamel, and at this stage it can be stopped with fluoride and good oral care. Once decay reaches the dentine, sensitivity to cold and sweet and darkening begin, and a filling is needed. When it reaches the nerve, spontaneous pain that is worse at night appears and root canal treatment is needed.

sections.html:
Bacteria in plaque on the teeth turn the sugars and starches we eat into acid, which dissolves minerals from the enamel. Saliva neutralises the acid and repairs the enamel. When you snack on sugar often through the day, there is no time for repair and decay begins.

In short

How often you have sugar matters more than how much. Sweet tea or juice sipped all day does more harm than a dessert eaten in one go.

sections.h: Stages of tooth decay and their treatment
sections.html:
StageSignsTreatment
1. White spot (mineral loss in enamel)No symptoms; dull, chalky white spotFluoride varnish, fluoride toothpaste, monitoring; reversible
2. Enamel decayBrown-black discolouration, slight roughnessA small white filling
3. Dentine decaySensitivity to cold and sweet, a hole, food trappingFilling; onlay or crown if a lot of tooth is lost
4. Decay reaching the nerveSpontaneous, throbbing pain, worse at nightRoot canal treatment, usually followed by a crown
5. AbscessSwelling, pain on biting, a pimple-like spot on the gum, feverRoot canal treatment or extraction; antibiotics if needed

sections.h: What are the signs of tooth decay?
sections.html:
• A white, brown or black spot on a tooth
  • A twinge with cold, heat or sweet food
  • A hole you can feel, or food always catching in the same place
  • Floss shredding at the same spot
  • A bad taste or bad breath from one area
  • Pain on biting, spontaneous pain or swelling (advanced stage)

sections.h: Hidden decay: between teeth and under fillings
sections.html:
Much decay starts where two teeth touch or at the edges of old fillings and crowns. You cannot see these areas in a mirror and they give no symptoms for a long time. Bitewing X-rays show this decay before it hurts, while it can still be treated with a small filling.

A check-up once a year is recommended if your decay risk is low, and every six months if it is high.

sections.h: Can tooth decay go away on its own?
sections.html:
Only the first stage, the white spot, can be stopped and reversed. Once a hole has formed in the enamel, decay does not heal; only its speed changes.

When a tooth that has hurt for a while suddenly stops hurting, that is not good news; it often means the nerve has died. Infection can then spread silently to the tip of the root.

sections.h: How can you prevent tooth decay?
sections.html:
• Brushing properly twice a day with fluoride toothpaste, especially at night
  • Cleaning between the teeth once a day
  • Keeping sugary food and drinks to mealtimes and drinking water between meals
  • Sugar-free (xylitol) gum after meals
  • Fissure sealants and regular fluoride for children's back teeth; see our children's dentistry guide
  • Regular check-ups and X-rays

At Dent32 in Beylikdüzü we treat decay early, removing as little tooth as possible. For a check-up, book an examination.

faq.q: Does decay need treating if it doesn't hurt?
faq.a: Yes. Decay usually does not hurt until it nears the nerve. A filling done at the painless stage avoids the need for root canal treatment and a crown.

faq.q: How do you know whether you need a filling or a root canal?
faq.a: The decision is based on the examination, X-rays and how the tooth responds to cold. Spontaneous pain that comes on at night usually means root canal treatment is needed.

faq.q: Can tooth decay cause bad breath?
faq.a: Yes. Food and bacteria collecting in decayed cavities can cause a bad smell and taste.

faq.q: Should decay in baby teeth be treated?
faq.a: Yes. Untreated decay in baby teeth causes pain and infection, and can harm the permanent tooth underneath and the space it needs.

title: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü: how many visits, who they suit and what affects the price
desc: Zirconia crowns in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: who they suit, how many visits and days they take, how much the tooth is reduced, how long they last and what affects the price.
lead: A zirconia crown is a strong, metal-free cap bonded over a worn, broken, discoloured or root-filled tooth. From examination to fitting, most patients need 3–4 appointments over about 1–2 weeks.

sections.html:
Zirconia is a high-strength ceramic. With no metal underneath, there's no dark line at the gum edge and light passes through in a way close to a natural tooth. That's why it's widely used for both front and back teeth.

For back teeth that carry chewing loads, solid (monolithic) zirconia is usually chosen; for front teeth, porcelain can be layered on top for a more lifelike look. We compare materials in our types of dental crowns article.

• Teeth weakened or broken by large fillings
  • Back teeth that need strengthening after root canal treatment
  • Severe discolouration that doesn't respond to whitening
  • Bridges to replace a missing tooth, or crowns on implants
  • People replacing old metal-backed crowns

If the tooth is largely sound and only the front surface needs an aesthetic change, a laminate veneer, which needs less reduction, may be a better choice.

The lab work between impressions and fitting usually takes 5–10 working days. It takes longer if root canal treatment, fillings or gum treatment are needed first. Because we're open at weekends, it's easier to fit appointments around your work.

In short

On healthy teeth, zirconia crowns are usually completed in 1–2 weeks over 3–4 visits.

sections.h: How much is the tooth reduced? Does it hurt?
sections.html:
For a zirconia crown, roughly 1–1.5 mm is usually removed around the tooth, more than for a veneer. It's done under local anaesthetic, so no pain is expected. There may be some hot and cold sensitivity for a few days afterwards; the temporary crown protects the tooth meanwhile.

sections.h: How long do zirconia crowns last?
sections.html:
Well-planned, well-maintained zirconia crowns can last many years. The main factors are the health of the tooth underneath, keeping the gum edge clean and whether you clench or grind. If you grind at night, a night guard protects your crowns.

You can see unretouched cases in our gallery and book at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü to discuss your own situation.

faq.q: Can zirconia crowns be done within a week?

faq.q: Do zirconia crowns change colour over time?
faq.a: No. Zirconia and porcelain surfaces don't stain permanently from tea, coffee or smoking, although surrounding natural teeth and the gum edge can.

faq.q: Should I whiten my teeth before getting crowns?
faq.a: The crown colour is matched to neighbouring natural teeth. If you want lighter teeth, whiten first; crowns don't whiten afterwards.

faq.q: Can a crowned tooth decay?
faq.a: The crown itself can't, but natural tooth at the gum edge can. Floss, interdental brushes and regular check-ups reduce the risk.

faq.q: Zirconia or porcelain?
faq.a: Compared with metal-backed porcelain, zirconia is more aesthetic and kinder to the gums. The choice depends on the tooth's position, bite forces and aesthetic expectations, and is made at the examination.

lead: Teeth whitening lightens tooth colour with peroxide gels under a dentist's supervision, either in a single session of about an hour in the clinic or with custom trays at home over 1–2 weeks. Depending on habits, results usually last 1–3 years.

sections.html:
Whitening works well on natural teeth yellowed by tea, coffee, smoking or age. Results can be more limited for antibiotic (tetracycline) or fluorosis staining; in those cases options such as veneers or bonding are discussed.

Important

Artificial surfaces such as fillings, crowns and veneers don't whiten. If you have old fillings in your front teeth, they may need replacing after whitening; we plan this from the start.

faq.q: Does whitening damage enamel?
faq.a: Whitening done under a dentist's supervision at the right strength doesn't permanently damage enamel. The risk lies mostly with overusing unsupervised products bought online.

faq.q: How many shades lighter will my teeth get?
faq.a: It depends on the starting shade and type of staining. Promising an exact shade in advance isn't honest; we record your shade together at the start.

faq.q: Does whitening hurt?
faq.a: No pain is expected during treatment. Some patients get brief, sharp twinges for 1–2 days afterwards that usually settle on their own.

faq.q: Will my crowns whiten too?
faq.a: No. Crowns, veneers and fillings don't whiten. If they're visible, they may need replacing to match the new shade.

faq.q: How often can it be repeated?
faq.a: For most patients the first result lasts for years. Short top-ups with home trays can be done if needed; frequent in-clinic sessions aren't recommended.

desc: For families looking for a children's dentist in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: when to have the first dental visit, fluoride varnish and fissure sealants, why baby teeth should be treated, and how to ease a child's fear of the dentist.
lead: A child's first dental visit should be when the first baby tooth appears, or by their first birthday at the latest. Regular check-ups and preventive care such as fluoride varnish and fissure sealants prevent most decay in baby and adult teeth.

sections.h: When should the first visit be?
sections.html:
The first baby tooth usually appears at around 6 months. A first visit then, or by age 1, is mainly to guide parents on feeding, bottle and dummy habits and brushing. Regular visits from an early age mean a child gets to know the dentist through routine check-ups rather than pain.

We describe how the first visit goes in your child's first dental visit.

sections.h: Baby teeth fall out anyway, so why treat them?
sections.html:
• Pain and infection: Untreated decay reaches the nerve, causing pain and abscesses.
  • Effect on adult teeth: Infection at the root of a baby tooth can affect the adult tooth developing underneath.
  • Holding space: If a baby tooth is lost early, the gap can close and the adult tooth comes in crooked. A space maintainer may be needed.
  • Eating and speech: Painful teeth make chewing and some sounds harder.

sections.h: How can a child's fear of the dentist be eased?
sections.html:
With children, we first introduce the instruments and the procedure in age-appropriate language, then show, then do (tell-show-do). Short appointments that end on a positive note make the next visit easier.

  • Don't present the visit as a reward or punishment, and avoid phrases like "it won't hurt" that can create anxiety.
  • Choose a time when your child isn't tired or hungry.
  • Try not to pass on your own dental anxiety.

Dent32 has a colourful treatment room designed for children. As the clinic is open at weekends, appointments can be planned without missing school.

faq.q: When should children start brushing?
faq.a: From the first tooth. Use a smear (rice-grain size) of fluoride toothpaste up to age 3 and a pea-sized amount from 3 to 6; parents should brush or supervise until about 7–8.

faq.q: Do fissure sealants harm the tooth?
faq.a: No. A sealant is a flowable material applied without drilling. It's painless and needs no anaesthetic.

faq.q: Can baby teeth have root canal treatment?
faq.a: Yes. When decay reaches the nerve of a baby tooth, a pulpotomy or baby-tooth root canal treatment can save it.

faq.q: What if my child won't cooperate?
faq.a: We first build trust with familiarisation visits. Sometimes treatment is split into several short sessions; for extensive treatment where cooperation isn't possible, we can refer for advanced sedation options.

title: Root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü: symptoms, number of visits and aftercare
desc: Root canal treatment in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: which symptoms mean you need one, how many visits it takes, whether it hurts, whether you need a crown afterwards and what to do about weekend toothache.
lead: Root canal treatment cleans out an inflamed nerve damaged by decay or trauma and seals the canals so the tooth can be kept. It's done under local anaesthetic and most teeth are finished in 1–2 visits.

sections.h: Which symptoms point to a root canal?
sections.html:
• Lingering pain after hot or cold
  • Spontaneous, throbbing pain that wakes you at night
  • Pain when biting or touching the tooth
  • A pimple-like bump on the gum (fistula) or facial swelling
  • A tooth that darkens after an injury

Sometimes the nerve dies without symptoms and the problem only shows on an X-ray. The decision is made after examination and X-rays.

1. The tooth is numbed with local anaesthetic and isolated from saliva.
  2. Decay is removed and the pulp chamber is reached.
  3. The canals are cleaned and shaped with fine instruments and rinsed with disinfecting solutions.
  4. Canal lengths are checked with X-rays or an electronic device.
  5. The canals are filled with a permanent material and the tooth is sealed.
How many visits?

Without infection, most teeth are done in one visit. With an abscess or severe inflammation, medication may be placed in the canals and the filling done at a second visit.

With effective anaesthesia you won't feel pain during treatment; only pressure and vibration. The tooth may be tender to bite on for 2–3 days afterwards; that's normal and painkillers help. If pain keeps increasing or swelling develops, contact the clinic.

General information is in our when do you need a root canal article.

sections.h: Do you need a crown afterwards?
sections.html:
ToothGeneral advice
Front teeth, little tooth lossA composite filling is often enough
Premolars and molarsA crown is usually recommended to prevent fracture
Teeth with major lossA post and crown may be needed

Root-filled teeth become more brittle over time. On back teeth, a zirconia crown protects against fracture and helps the tooth last.

sections.h: What if the root canal fails?
sections.html: Root canal treatment has a high success rate, but infection can return years later. Re-treatment is tried first; if needed, root-end surgery (apicectomy) is done. If the tooth can't be saved, it's extracted and replaced with an implant or bridge.

sections.h: When toothache starts at the weekend
sections.html: Pain that needs a root canal often starts at the worst time: at night or at the weekend. Dent32 is open seven days a week, so we can see a painful tooth the same day and, if needed, carry out first aid (opening the tooth to relieve pressure). faq.q: How long does a root canal take?
faq.a: Usually 30–60 minutes for front teeth and 60–90 minutes for multi-canal molars, depending on the number of canals and inflammation.

faq.q: Can antibiotics replace a root canal?
faq.a: No. Antibiotics can help control spreading infection and swelling, but they don't clean out the inflamed tissue inside the tooth. Pain may ease temporarily but the problem remains.

faq.q: Will a root-filled tooth last for life?
faq.a: A properly treated and well-restored tooth can last many years, often for life.

faq.q: Root canal or extraction?
faq.a: Keeping the natural tooth is preferred where possible. If the tooth is badly broken or the root is cracked, extraction and an implant may be more predictable; the decision is made at the examination.

title: Gum treatment in Beylikdüzü: bleeding, recession and deep cleaning
desc: Gum treatment in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: causes of bleeding and receding gums, gingivitis versus periodontitis, deep cleaning, the effect of smoking and diabetes, home care and check-up intervals.
lead: Bleeding gums are the earliest sign of gum disease. At the early stage (gingivitis) it reverses fully with professional cleaning and good home care; at the advanced stage (periodontitis), deep cleaning and regular maintenance stop it progressing.

sections.html:
• Bleeding when brushing or flossing
  • Red, swollen, tender gums
  • Persistent bad breath or a bad taste
  • Receding gums and teeth that look longer
  • Loose teeth or widening gaps

In smokers, gum blood vessels constrict so bleeding is less visible, which can delay diagnosis.

GingivitisPeriodontitis
Tissue affectedGums onlyGums, supporting tissue and bone
SignsBleeding, rednessRecession, pockets, looseness, bone loss
Reversible?FullyLost bone usually doesn't return; progression is stopped
TreatmentScale and polish plus home careDeep cleaning, surgery if needed, regular maintenance

1. Examination and charting: Pocket depths are measured and bone levels assessed on X-rays.
  2. Scale and polish: Tartar and plaque are removed from the tooth surfaces and polished.
  3. Deep cleaning (root planing): Tartar below the gum line is removed under local anaesthetic and root surfaces smoothed.
  4. Re-evaluation: The gum response is measured after a few weeks; if deep pockets remain, surgical options are discussed.
  5. Maintenance: Check-ups and cleaning, usually every 3–6 months depending on risk.

Smoking and uncontrolled diabetes are the strongest risk factors for gum disease: they speed it up and reduce the response to treatment. The link with diabetes works both ways: treating gum inflammation can also help blood sugar control.

A similar inflammation (peri-implantitis) can develop around implants, so implant aftercare and regular check-ups matter.

• Brushing twice a day for two minutes with a soft brush
  • Floss or correctly sized interdental brushes between teeth
  • Short-term antiseptic mouthwash when your dentist recommends it
  • Stopping or cutting down smoking

We explain the causes in more detail in bleeding and receding gums. You can book a gum check at our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Will bleeding gums stop on their own?
faq.a: Usually not, unless the plaque and tartar causing it are removed. Stopping brushing makes it worse; keep brushing gently and come in for a check.

faq.q: Do receded gums grow back?
faq.a: Not on their own. Progression can be stopped, and in suitable cases surgery such as a gum graft can cover the exposed root.

faq.q: Does deep cleaning hurt?
faq.a: It's done under local anaesthetic, so no pain is expected during treatment. There may be some tenderness for a few days.

faq.q: Can gum disease cause tooth loss?
faq.a: Yes. Advanced periodontitis is one of the main causes of tooth loss in adults. Early treatment is the most effective way to keep your teeth.

sections.h: How long do veneers last and how do you look after them?
sections.html:
Well-planned, well-maintained veneers can last many years. Not biting hard objects (nutshells, pens, nails) with your front teeth, wearing a night guard if you grind, and six-monthly check-ups all extend their life.

faq.q: Is the whole tooth cut down for a veneer?
faq.a: No. Only about 0.3–0.7 mm is removed from the front surface; in some cases no reduction is needed.

faq.q: Can veneers fall off?
faq.a: Properly bonded veneers don't come off easily. Biting hard objects with front teeth and grinding at night increase the risk of chipping or debonding.

faq.q: Will my teeth be sensitive after veneers?
faq.a: When reduction stays within the enamel, sensitivity is usually mild and temporary.

faq.q: Can I choose any shade I like?
faq.a: Yes, a wide range of shades is possible. For a natural look we suggest a shade that suits your skin tone, the whites of your eyes and your gums; we decide together at the try-in.

sections.html:
Each year the Turkish Dental Association (TDB) publishes a minimum fee schedule for dentists in private practice. It sets a floor for procedures; clinics set their own prices above it according to materials and service.

If a quote is far below the schedule, ask specifically which materials will be used and what is and isn't included in the plan.

sections.h: The hidden cost of cheap treatment
sections.html:
The most expensive dental treatment is the one that has to be redone. An ill-fitting crown can lead to gum disease, an incompletely cleaned canal to re-infection, and a poorly positioned implant to bone loss. In those cases, the cost of re-treatment is added to what you paid first.

1. Examination: Oral tissues and remaining teeth are assessed; extractions or fillings are done first if needed.

  4. Try-in: Teeth set in wax are tried in; appearance and speech are checked.

A new denture can feel large and foreign at first. Slight changes in speech, extra saliva and sore spots are normal. Most people adapt within 2–4 weeks.

  • In the first days, eat soft food in small bites, chewing on both sides together.
  • Reading aloud helps you get used to speaking.
  • If you get a sore spot, don't file the denture yourself; come in for an adjustment.

• Take it out after every meal and brush it under running water; use soap or denture cleaner rather than toothpaste.
  • Take it out at night and store it in clean water or a cleaning-tablet solution so your tissues can rest.
  • Don't use hot water; it can warp the denture.
  • Clean your palate, tongue and gums with a soft brush too.

After tooth loss, the jawbone gradually shrinks, so a denture that fits well at first can loosen over the years. It then needs relining or replacing. A loose denture causes sores and chewing problems, so a yearly check is recommended.

Important

A remote assessment is preliminary information only. The final plan and cost are confirmed after an examination and any necessary imaging at the clinic.

Detailed planning tips are in our dental treatment in Istanbul guide.

So that your dentist at home can follow up your treatment, ask for a written summary of the procedures, copies of your X-rays and, if you had implants, the brand and model of the implant used. This makes any future maintenance or part replacement much easier.

For all our treatments, see our dentist in Beylikdüzü guide or the home page of our dental clinic in Beylikdüzü.

faq.q: Do the dentists speak English?
faq.a: Yes, examinations and treatment can be conducted in English. Just mention that you'd like to communicate in English when booking.

faq.q: Can I get my treatment plan in English?
faq.a: Yes. Findings, options and costs can be shared in writing in English.

faq.q: What should I do if there's a problem after I go home?
faq.a: Contact us on WhatsApp with photos and a description. If needed, we'll share information to guide a dentist where you are.

faq.q: Do I need my passport or ID for the appointment?
faq.a: Your ID or passport details are needed to create your health record; just bring it with you to the appointment.

title: Choosing a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: what to look for
desc: How to choose a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü or anywhere in Istanbul: the examination, a written treatment plan and price, the dental team, sterilisation, access and aftercare.
lead: The quickest way to judge a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü is to look at how thorough the first examination is, whether the treatment plan and cost are given in writing, and how follow-up is handled after treatment.

sections.h: Why does choosing the right clinic matter?
sections.html:
Many dental treatments are hard to reverse: enamel that is removed doesn't grow back, an extracted tooth can't be put back, and an implant can't easily be repositioned once it's in the bone. That's why the quality of planning should weigh as much as price or convenience.

There are many dental clinics, polyclinics and private practices in Beylikdüzü and the neighbouring districts of Esenyurt, Büyükçekmece and Avcılar. With so much choice, it helps to have concrete criteria to compare them. The sections below summarise them.

sections.h: What should happen at the first examination?
sections.html:
A good first examination isn't limited to the tooth that hurts. The whole mouth, the gums, your bite and any existing fillings or crowns are assessed, with a panoramic X-ray or 3D CT scan if needed.

  • Findings explained: You should be shown what the X-ray shows, in plain language.
  • Options presented: Most problems have more than one solution (e.g. implant, bridge or removable denture). The pros and cons of each should be discussed.
  • No pressure: You should be given time to think, not pushed into starting major treatment on the same day.
  • Room for questions: The time a dentist gives your questions says a lot about communication during treatment.

sections.h: Why a written treatment plan and price matter
sections.html:
Verbal quotes often change as extra items are added during treatment. A written plan makes clear from the start what will be done to each tooth, how many visits it will take and what each item costs.

What the plan should includeWhy it matters
Procedures, tooth by toothYou know exactly what you're paying for
Materials and brandsE.g. implant brand, zirconia or e.max
Possible additional proceduresBone grafts, sinus lifts or root canals don't come as a surprise
Number of visits and timelineYou can plan work, travel and daily life
Check-ups and follow-upThe scope of aftercare is clear

At Dent32 we share the findings, options and an approximate cost in writing after the examination. We explain what shapes the cost in our article on dental implant cost factors.

sections.h: The dental team and their areas of focus
sections.html:
You're entitled to know in advance which dentist will carry out which treatment. Orthodontics, implant surgery, aesthetic dentistry and children's dentistry each call for different experience. When several disciplines plan together under one roof, cases that need, say, orthodontics followed by crowns run more smoothly.

We introduce our team and how we work on our about page. You can also see previous cases in our before-and-after gallery.

sections.h: How can you tell sterilisation is taken seriously?
sections.html:
• Instruments opened from sterile pouches for every patient
  • Single-use items (needles, gloves, suction tips) changed for every patient
  • Surfaces of the dental unit disinfected between patients
  • A dedicated sterilisation area in the clinic

Don't hesitate to ask about these; a careful clinic will be happy to answer.

sections.h: Access, opening days and urgent problems
sections.html:
Implant or orthodontic treatment involves several appointments over months. Easy access to the clinic and appointments outside your working hours make it easier to stay on schedule.

Dent32 is in Barış Mahallesi, Beylikdüzü, on the E-5 service road at Ginza Lavinya, and is open seven days a week. For toothache that starts in the evening or at the weekend, see our emergency toothache guide.

In short

A thorough examination, a written plan and cost, clarity about who treats you, visible hygiene standards and proper aftercare are the five things to look for when choosing a dental clinic in Beylikdüzü or anywhere in Istanbul.

faq.q: Is there a difference between a dental clinic and a dental polyclinic?
faq.a: In Türkiye, an oral and dental health polyclinic is a licensed facility where several dentists work together and specific requirements are met; a private practice usually has one dentist. In everyday language "dental clinic" is used for both. For patients, what matters most is the dentist's experience, planning and hygiene.

faq.q: Do I have to start treatment at the first visit?
faq.a: No. The first visit is for understanding your situation and discussing options. It's perfectly normal to take the plan home, think it over, or get a second opinion.

faq.q: Can I get a price over the phone or on WhatsApp?
faq.a: If you send photos and X-rays we can give preliminary information, but the final plan and cost are confirmed after a clinical examination and any necessary imaging.

faq.q: Do you see patients from outside Beylikdüzü?
faq.a: Yes. We have patients from Esenyurt, Büyükçekmece, Avcılar and other districts of Istanbul, as well as from abroad. We can plan appointments to keep the number of visits down.

title: Dental implants in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: from examination to final tooth
desc: How dental implant treatment works at a clinic in Beylikdüzü, Istanbul: examination and CT scan, implant surgery, healing time, the final crown and check-ups, step by step.
lead: Dental implant treatment follows five basic steps: examination and CT scan, planning, placing the implant, waiting for it to fuse with the bone, and fitting the final tooth. For a single tooth, the process takes 3 to 6 months for most patients.

sections.html:
Implant planning starts with measuring the bone. A panoramic X-ray gives an overview, but the width and height of the bone and its distance from the nerve canal and sinus can only be measured reliably with a 3D cone-beam CT scan.

Gum health, neighbouring teeth, your bite and your general health (medication, diabetes, smoking) are assessed at the same time. Any decay or gum inflammation is treated before the implant.

sections.h: 2. Planning: how many implants, which brand, what kind of tooth?
sections.html:
The implant's diameter, length and angle are planned from the CT data. A single missing tooth is usually replaced with one implant and a crown; several missing teeth with implant-supported bridges; a whole arch with solutions such as All-on-Four.

SituationCommon solution
One missing toothOne implant + zirconia or porcelain crown
Two or three adjacent missing teethBridge on two implants
No teeth in the jawFixed bridge on 4–6 implants or an implant-retained denture
Insufficient boneImplant after bone graft or sinus lift

For full-arch options, see our All-on-Four guide and our article on implant-supported dentures.

The procedure is done under local anaesthetic. The gum is opened, a site is prepared in the bone and the implant is placed; the area is then stitched or a healing cap is fitted. A single implant usually takes 30–60 minutes.

Most patients feel pressure rather than pain. Mild swelling and tenderness for a few days are normal. We explain what to do afterwards in our implant aftercare guide.

The implant takes about 2–3 months to fuse in the lower jaw and 3–6 months in the upper jaw. A temporary tooth can be worn in visible areas during this time, so you're not left with a gap.

In some suitable cases the implant can be placed in the same visit as the extraction (immediate implant), with a temporary tooth on the same day. We cover when this is possible in how long implant treatment takes.

Once the implant has fused, an impression is taken (digital scan or conventional) and the final tooth is made. After a try-in, the crown or bridge is fixed to the implant. A few check-ups follow in the first year, then an examination and professional clean every six months.

How many visits?

For a single implant, 4–6 visits are enough for most patients: examination and CT, implant surgery, stitch check, impression, try-in, and fitting the final tooth.

sections.h: Questions to ask before getting an implant
sections.html:
• Which implant brand will be used, and will spare parts still be available years from now?
  • Is there enough bone, or will a graft or sinus lift be needed?
  • What material will the tooth on top be made of?
  • Will I have a temporary tooth while the implant heals?
  • What will the follow-up schedule be?

At Dent32 we plan implant treatment with an examination and CT scan and give you the plan in writing. See our implant treatment section or book an appointment. If you're travelling from abroad, our planning guide explains how to organise visits.

faq.q: How long does implant treatment take in Istanbul?
faq.a: With healthy, sufficient bone, a single implant is usually completed in 3–4 months. If a bone graft or sinus lift is needed, it can take 6–9 months overall.

faq.q: Am I put to sleep for implant surgery?
faq.a: Most implants are placed under local anaesthetic without sedation. If many implants are planned or you're very anxious, sedation options can be discussed.

faq.q: Can I go back to work after an implant?
faq.a: After a single implant most patients return to normal activities the next day. After more extensive surgery a few days' rest may be advised.

faq.q: Can I have implants if I've lost bone?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. If bone volume is insufficient, a bone graft or sinus lift can prepare the site; in some cases short or angled implants avoid the need for extra surgery.

title: What affects the cost of dental implants?
desc: What determines the price of a dental implant: implant brand, the crown on top, bone grafts and sinus lifts, number of implants and planning. What to check when comparing quotes.
lead: The cost of a dental implant isn't a single number: the implant brand, the material of the tooth on top, additional procedures such as a bone graft or sinus lift, and the total number of implants together determine the price.

sections.h: Why can't everyone be quoted the same price?
sections.html:
Asking "how much is an implant?" is a bit like asking "how much is a car?": without knowing the model, the specification and the extras, a single answer would be misleading. Two patients may both need "one implant", but one needs only the implant and crown while the other also needs an extraction, a bone graft and a temporary tooth.

Single prices quoted over the phone or online often cover only the screw; the crown and extra procedures are added later. When comparing, look at a written plan for the whole treatment.

sections.h: The main factors that set the price
sections.html:
FactorEffect on cost
Implant brand and systemSystems with strong long-term clinical data and good parts availability usually cost more
The crown on topZirconia, porcelain or e.max, plus the type of abutment (connecting part)
Additional surgeryExtraction, bone graft, membrane, sinus lift
Number of implantsSingle tooth, bridge or full-arch plan
Temporary toothWearing a temporary tooth in visible areas while healing
Imaging and planningCT scan, and where needed digital planning and a surgical guide

sections.h: Does the implant brand really matter?
sections.html:
Yes, but not simply because "expensive is better". What matters is that the brand is backed by research, that spare parts will still be available years later when a crown needs replacing, and that the dentist is experienced with that system.

With an unknown or discontinued system, finding compatible parts later can be difficult. That's why the implant brand should be stated in your treatment plan.

sections.h: How do bone grafts and sinus lifts affect the cost?
sections.html:
If a tooth was lost long ago, the bone shrinks over time. Without enough bone, a graft or, in the upper back jaw, a sinus lift may be needed before or during implant placement. These add to both cost and overall time. See our article on bone grafts and sinus lifts for details.

Tip

If you have a tooth that needs to come out, discuss the implant plan at the extraction appointment. In some cases the implant can be placed at the same visit, or steps can be taken to limit bone loss.

sections.h: What to watch out for with very low prices
sections.html:
• Ask whether the price covers only the screw or also the abutment and crown.
  • Ask for the implant brand and crown material in writing.
  • Be wary of a final plan made without a CT scan.
  • Ask how check-ups and any complications will be handled.

An implant is meant to stay in your mouth for many years. A small saving at the start can turn into a much larger cost if it needs to be redone.

sections.h: How is the price set at Dent32?
